BURSEVI:v5p42/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p42/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p42/r1.claim: Bee inspiration resembles guidance for spiritual travelers: they withdraw to mountains like the Prophet’s retreats at Hira, maintain cleanliness, and avoid polluted places and foods.
BURSEVI:v5p42/r1.anchor: خص النحل بالوحي وهو الإلهام والرشد من بين سائر الحيوانات

BURSEVI:v5p42/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p42/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p42/r2.claim: The fruits of the body are righteous deeds, of the soul ascetic discipline and struggle against desire, of the heart renouncing the world for God, and of the secret witnessing truth and drawing near.
BURSEVI:v5p42/r2.anchor: وثمرات البدن الأعمال الصالحة وثمرات النفوس الرياضات والمجاهدات

BURSEVI:v5p42/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p42/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p42/r3.claim: God’s command to bees to eat all fruits parallels the command to believers to eat wholesome things and act righteously.

QUSHAYRI:v2p162/r3.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p162/r3.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p162/r3.claim: Divine favor is not distributed by measurable merit: the unremarkable bee yields healing honey, while humans of excellent form and intellect may suffer inward estrangement.
QUSHAYRI:v2p162/r3.anchor: ومع ذلك جعل منه العسل الذي هو شفاء للناس

QUSHAYRI:v2p162/r4.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p162/r4.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p162/r4.claim: God hides precious things in lowly containers—silk in worms, honey in bees, pearls in shells, and metals or gems in stone; likewise He places knowledge and love in fallible believers.
QUSHAYRI:v2p162/r4.anchor: أجرى سنته أن يخفي كل شيء عزيز في شيء حقير

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p559/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p559/r1.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p559/r1.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī explicitly takes بيوتا as the hexagonal cells built by bees and construes eating from every fruit as from those they desire.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p559/r1.anchor: قال الزمخشري: أي ابني البيوت ثم كلي من كل ثمرة تشتهيها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p559/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p559/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p559/r9.claim: The delay conveyed by ثم fits honey gathering after nest-building; كلي is an imperative coordinated with اتخذي, and كل الثمرات is a general expression restricted to customary fruits.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p559/r9.anchor: وتقتضي ثم المهلة والتراخي بين الاتخاذ والأكل الذي تدخر منه العسل، فلذلك كان العطف بثم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p560/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p560/r1.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p560/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya says the bee eats blossoms from trees.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p560/r1.anchor: قال ابن عطية: إنما تأكل النوار من الأشجار

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p560/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p560/r2.speaker: أبو عبد الله الرازي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p560/r2.claim: Al-Rāzī proposes that honey forms from subtle particles arising in the air like ترنجبين, which bees collect from flowers and leaves and store as food; on this account من marks origin, not a part.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p560/r2.anchor: وقال أبو عبد الله الرازي ما ملخصه: يحدث الله تعالى في الهواء ظلا كثيرا يجتمع منه أجزاء محسوسة مثل الترنجبين

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p560/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p560/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p560/r3.claim: من كل الثمرات most naturally means a portion: the bee takes from good trees and fragrant leaves, producing honey within itself.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p560/r3.anchor: وظاهر من في قوله: من كل الثمرات أنها للتبعيض، فتأكل من الأشجار الطيبة والأوراق العطرة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p560/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p560/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p560/r4.claim: The fāʾ in فاسلكي naturally places flight along the bee's routes immediately after eating; bees may migrate far for forage and return home. Other readings take the paths as inspired honey-making methods or the divine processes that transform food into honey.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p560/r4.anchor: وظاهر العطف بالفاء في فاسلكي أنه بعقيب الأكل أي: فإذا أكلت فاسلكي سبل ربك، أي طرق ربك إلى بيوتك راجعة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p560/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p560/r5.speaker: مجاهد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p560/r5.claim: Mujāhid says ذللا means the routes are easy and not rugged for the bee; it is then an adverbial state of the Lord's paths. Qatāda instead says obedient and compliant, and Ibn Zayd says the bees follow beekeepers as they move them.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p560/r5.anchor: وقال مجاهد: ذللا غير متوعرة عليها سبيل تسلكه، فعلى هذا ذللا حال من سبيل ربك

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p560/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p560/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p560/r6.claim: The mention of a drink from the bees' bellies recounts the result of nest-making, eating, and following the routes, just as milk and fruit drinks were benefits of livestock and trees.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p560/r6.anchor: ثمرة هذا الاتخاذ والأكل والسلوك وهو قوله: يخرج من بطونها شراب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p561/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p561/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p561/r1.claim: Most commentators say honey exits the bee's mouth, the endpoint of its route; al-Ḥarīrī's line calls praise 'honey-licking' and blame 'wasp vomit,' both terms implying a mouth.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p561/r1.anchor: والجمهور على أنه يخرج من أفواهها وهو مبدأ الغاية الأخيرة ولذلك قال الحريري

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p561/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p561/r2.speaker: علي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p561/r2.claim: ʿAlī belittles worldly life by saying humanity's finest clothing is a worm's saliva and finest drink is a bee's residue; another saying of his calls honey fly vomit, implying an exit other than the mouth.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p561/r2.anchor: وروي عن علي كرم الله وجهه أنه قال في تحقير الدنيا: أشرف لباس ابن آدم فيها لعاب دودة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p561/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p561/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p561/r3.claim: A tale says Solomon, Alexander, and Aristotle built glass hives to watch where honey emerged, but the bees coated the glass with mud and blocked the view.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p561/r3.anchor: وحكي أن سليمان عليه السلام، والإسكندر، وأرسطاطاليس، صنعوا لها بيوتا من زجاج

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p561/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p561/r4.speaker: الحسن
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p561/r4.claim: Al-Ḥasan calls honey wheat's pulp with the bee's saliva and thus treats it as mouth secretion; another view calls the mouth a belly because it is hidden within.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p561/r4.anchor: وقال الحسن: لباب البر بلعاب النحل بخالص السمن ما عابه مسلم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p561/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p561/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p561/r5.claim: Honey's colors and taste vary with bees' temperaments and forage; a hadith mentions bees feeding on ʿurfut, and another view links colors to young, middle-aged, and mature bees.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p561/r5.anchor: واختلاف ألوانه بالبياض والصفرة والحمرة والسواد، وذلك لاختلاف طباع النحل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p561/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p561/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p561/r6.claim: The pronoun in فيه returns to honey, a familiar medicine, though it does not cure every illness; شفاء is indefinite either for magnification ('remarkable healing') or generality ('some healing').
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p561/r6.anchor: والظاهر عود الضمير فيه إلى الشراب وهو العسل، لأنه شفاء من جملة الأشفية والأدوية المشهورة النافعة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p561#2/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p561#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p561#2/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, al-Ḥasan, Mujāhid, al-Ḍaḥḥāk, al-Farrāʾ, and Ibn Kaysān reportedly make the pronoun in فيه refer to the Qur'an as healing; al-Naḥḥās approves, while Ibn al-ʿArabī rejects the report as contextually and rationally unsound.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p561#2/r1.anchor: وروي عن ابن عباس، والحسن، ومجاهد، والضحاك، والفراء، وابن كيسان: أن الضمير في فيه عائد على القرآن

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p561#2/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p561#2/r2.speaker: ابن العربي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p561#2/r2.claim: Ibn al-ʿArabī doubts this attribution and rejects the Qur'anic interpretation: the whole context concerns honey, with no mention of Qur'an.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p561#2/r2.anchor: قال القاضي أبو بكر بن العربي: أرى هذا القول لا يصح نقله عن هؤلاء، ولو صح نقلا لم يصح عقلا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p561#2/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p561#2/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p561#2/r3.claim: The remarkable cells, diverse sour, bitter, and harmful flowers and leaves the bee eats, and its obedience to leader and keeper invite contemplation, fitting the verse's conclusion.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p561#2/r3.anchor: ولما كان أمر النحل عجيبا في بنائها تلك البيوت المسدسة، وفي أكلها من أنواع الأزهار والأوراق الحامض والمر والضار

FARRA:v2p109/r5.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p109/r5.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p109/r5.claim: ذللا is an adjective for the paths; alternatively it describes bees made docile so drink can emerge from their bodies.

FARRA:v2p109/r6.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p109/r6.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p109/r6.claim: شفاء للناس refers either to honey as medicine or, with its pronoun taken as the Quran, to its explanation of lawful and forbidden matters.
FARRA:v2p109/r6.anchor: يعني العسل دواء ويقال (فيه شفاء للناس) يراد بالهاء القرآن

DURR-FULL:v5p142#2/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p142#2/r11.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v5p142#2/r11.claim: Mujahid says the bee's paths are routes without difficult terrain wherever it travels; Qatadah glosses the bee as obedient, while Ibn Zayd says it is led wherever its owner wants.
DURR-FULL:v5p142#2/r11.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله: {فاسلكي سبل ربك ذللا} قال: طرقا لا يتوعر عليها مكان

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p406/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p406/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p406/r6.claim: The command to eat is inspired after the command to make homes; مِن is partitive because bees eat only some flowers from all fruits.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p406/r6.anchor: أن كلي، فعطف كلي على اتخذي، ومن للتبعيض

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p406/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p406/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p406/r7.claim: Subl means routes of flight and travel; they belong to the Lord because He created and enabled them.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p406/r7.anchor: من حيث هي ملكه وخلقه التي يسر لك ربك

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p406/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p406/r8.speaker: قتادة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p406/r8.claim: Qatada takes ذللا as an adjective of the bees: obedient and guided along their way.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p406/r8.anchor: أي مطيعة منقادة لما يسرت له، قاله قتادة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p406/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p406/r9.speaker: ابن زيد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p406/r9.claim: Ibn Zayd says people go out for forage and the bees follow them.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p406/r9.anchor: فهم يخرجون بالنحل ينتجعون وهي تتبعهم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p406/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p406/r10.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p406/r10.claim: Alternatively ذللا describes the paths as smooth and straight; Mujahid says the bee encounters no rough path.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p406/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p406/r11.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p406/r11.claim: The taming of bees recalls the Qur’anic description of livestock made manageable for people.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p406/r11.anchor: وقرأ أولم يروا أنا خلقنا لهم مما عملت أيدينا أنعاما فهم لها مالكون وذللناها لهم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p406/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p406/r12.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p406/r12.claim: Most people say honey comes out of bees’ mouths, though an account attributed to Ali’s remarks about worldly goods suggests it comes from elsewhere.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p406/r12.anchor: وجمهور الناس على أن العسل يخرج من أفواه النحل

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p406/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p406/r13.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p406/r13.claim: Honey’s colors and flavors vary with different bees and sources of forage; Zaynab described the bees’ forage to explain a smell like maghafir.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p406/r13.anchor: في العسل بحسب اختلاف النحل والمراعي وقد يختلف طعمه بحسب اختلاف المراعي

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p406/r14.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p406/r14.speaker: الجمهور
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p406/r14.claim: The pronoun in فيه شفاء refers to honey, but the statement promises healing in some cases and conditions, as with other medicines, not every disease in every person.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p406/r14.anchor: ولا يقتضي العموم في كل علة وفي كل إنسان

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p406/r15.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p406/r15.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p406/r15.claim: The verse highlights honey as a medicine that often heals and is used alongside other remedies in drinks and compounds.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p406/r15.anchor: ففائدة الآية إخبار منبه منه في أنه دواء كما كثر الشفاء به

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p406/r16.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p406/r16.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p406/r16.claim: Ibn Umar reportedly treated every complaint with honey, including applying it to boils while reciting the verse.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p406/r16.anchor: إلا تداوى بالعسل، حتى إنه كان يدهن به الدمل والضرحة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p406#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p406#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p406#2/r1.claim: Ibn Umar’s practice implies that he considered honey healing in all cases.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p406#2/r1.anchor: وهذا يقتضي أنه يرى الشفاء به على العموم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p406#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p406#2/r2.speaker: مجاهد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p406#2/r2.claim: Mujahid says the pronoun in فيه شفاء refers to the Qur’an, which contains healing.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p406#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p406#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p406#2/r3.claim: The author ridicules an esoteric claim that bees represent the Prophet’s family and honey represents the Qur’an and wisdom.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p406#2/r3.anchor: وذهب قوم من أهل الجهالة إلى أن هذه الآية إنما يراد بها أهل البيت ورجال بني هاشم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p406#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p406#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p406#2/r4.claim: At al-Mansur’s gathering, a man mocked that interpretation by asking that the ruler’s food and drink come from the bellies of Hashemites, exposing its absurdity.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p406#2/r4.anchor: جعل الله طعامك وشرابك مما يخرج من بطون بني هاشم، فأضحك الحاضرين

MUQATIL:16:68-70/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:16:68-70/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:16:68-70/r2.claim: The bee follows paths God has made easy through mountains and trees; its honey is white, yellow, or red and cures some illnesses.
MUQATIL:16:68-70/r2.anchor: { ذللا }؛ لأن الله تعالى ذلل لها طرقها حيثما توجهت،

MUQATIL:16:68-70/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:16:68-70/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:16:68-70/r3.claim: The bee and its honey are a sign for people who reflect on God's oneness.
MUQATIL:16:68-70/r3.anchor: { إن في ذلك لآية } ، يعني فيما ذكر من أمر النحل وما يخرج من بطونها لعبرة،

ASAD-NOTES:16:intro/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:16:intro/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:16:intro/r2.claim: The title points to the bee as an instance of divine creativity, while evidence of God's purposeful activity culminates in the ethical injunctions of verse 90.
ASAD-NOTES:16:intro/r2.anchor: the evidence of the Creator's purposeful activity that provides the subject-matter of most of this surah

STUDYQURAN:16:intro/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:16:intro/r7.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:16:intro/r7.claim: The surah takes its name from its account of God's revelation to the bee.
STUDYQURAN:16:intro/r7.anchor: The sūrah takes its name from the discussion of God’s revelation to the bee in vv. 68–69.

STUDYQURAN:16:intro/r11.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:16:intro/r11.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:16:intro/r11.claim: It also presents four divinely given drinks: water, milk, drink from vine fruit, and honey.
STUDYQURAN:16:intro/r11.anchor: Later the sūrah mentions the four drinks with which God has blessed human beings

TABATABAI:16:69-70/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:16:69-70/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:16:69-70/r1.claim: The bee’s paths lead back to its hives to store honey gathered from fruits, and are attributed to the Lord because the bee follows divine inspiration.
TABATABAI:16:69-70/r1.anchor: تفريعه على الأمر بالأكل يؤيد أن المراد به رجوعها إلى بيوتها لتودع فيها ما هيأته

TABATABAI:16:69-70/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:16:69-70/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:16:69-70/r2.claim: The drink from the bees is honey of varied colors, from white and yellow through bright red to shades near black, and it heals most illnesses.
TABATABAI:16:69-70/r2.anchor: بالبياض والصفرة والحمرة الناصعة وما يميل إلى السواد

TABATABAI:16:69-70/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:16:69-70/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:16:69-70/r3.claim: The author says the bee’s complex social life and the properties of its honey exceed the scope of this book and directs readers to specialist research.
TABATABAI:16:69-70/r3.anchor: وتفصيل القول في حياة النحلة هذه الحشرة الفطنة التي بنت حياتها على مدنية عجيبة

TABATABAI:16:69-70/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:16:69-70/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:16:69-70/r4.claim: The signs are matched to different faculties: reviving earth suits listeners as admonition, fruit suits reasoned inference from ordered systems to one manager, and bee life suits reflective thought because its details are subtle.
TABATABAI:16:69-70/r4.anchor: وقد اختلف التعبير بذلك في هذه الآيات فخص الآية في إحياء الأرض بعد موتها

TABATABAI:16:69-70/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:16:69-70/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:16:69-70/r5.claim: The surah alternates its address between the Prophet and polytheists, out of compassion for people who do not know and turning away from those who reject and deny.
TABATABAI:16:69-70/r5.anchor: وعمدتها في هذه الآيات ترجع إلى خطاب المشركين رحمة لهم وإشفاقا بحالهم وهم لا يعلمون

TABRISI:16:66-70#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:16:66-70#2/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:16:66-70#2/r3.claim: The healing pronoun can refer to honey or the Qur’an; with honey, ‘healing’ is predicated through the prepositional phrase, while the Qur’an reading raises a different syntactic question.
TABRISI:16:66-70#2/r3.anchor: الهاء في قوله فيه شفاء للناس قيل يعود إلى الشراب وهو العسل وقيل يعود إلى القرآن

TABRISI:16:67-69/r14.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:16:67-69/r14.speaker: مجاهد
TABRISI:16:67-69/r14.claim: The bee’s ‘tamed’ paths are made smooth, open, and wide for travel.
TABRISI:16:67-69/r14.anchor: صفة للسبل وهي منصوبة على الحال وهو قول مجاهد

TABRISI:16:67-69/r15.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:16:67-69/r15.speaker: قتادة
TABRISI:16:67-69/r15.claim: Alternatively, ‘tamed’ describes the bees as obedient, submissive, and made subject to God.
TABRISI:16:67-69/r15.anchor: وقيل ذللا أي مطيعة لله منقادة مسخرة ويكون من صفة النحل عن قتادة

TABRISI:16:67-69/r16.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:16:67-69/r16.speaker: author
TABRISI:16:67-69/r16.claim: Honey varies in color—white, yellow, or reddish—because bees take from different plants and flowers; although it comes from the belly, they release it from the mouth like saliva.
TABRISI:16:67-69/r16.anchor: وهو العسل فإن ألوانه مختلفة لأن منه ما هو شديد البياض ومنه ما هو أصفر ومنه ما يضرب إلى الحمرة

TABRISI:16:69-70/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:16:69-70/r1.speaker: قتادة
TABRISI:16:69-70/r1.claim: Honey heals illnesses, according to Qatāda; al-Suddī and al-Ḥasan specify diseases for which honey is an effective remedy.

TABRISI:16:69-70/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:16:69-70/r2.speaker: السدي
TABRISI:16:69-70/r2.claim: Honey heals illnesses, according to Qatāda; al-Suddī and al-Ḥasan specify diseases for which honey is an effective remedy.
TABRISI:16:69-70/r2.anchor: وقيل معناه فيه شفاء للأوجاع التي شفاؤها فيه عن السدي والحسن

TABRISI:16:69-70/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:16:69-70/r3.speaker: الحسن
TABRISI:16:69-70/r3.claim: Honey heals illnesses, according to Qatāda; al-Suddī and al-Ḥasan specify diseases for which honey is an effective remedy.
TABRISI:16:69-70/r3.anchor: فيه شفاء للأوجاع التي شفاؤها فيه عن السدي والحسن

TABRISI:16:69-70/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:16:69-70/r4.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
TABRISI:16:69-70/r4.claim: Ibn Masʿūd says to use the two cures: the Qur’an and honey.
TABRISI:16:69-70/r4.anchor: وروي عن عبد الله بن مسعود أنه قال عليكم بالشفاءين القرآن والعسل

TABRISI:16:69-70/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:16:69-70/r5.speaker: مجاهد
TABRISI:16:69-70/r5.claim: Mujāhid takes the pronoun in ‘in it is healing’ to refer to the Qur’an, whose law, prohibitions, legal opinions, and rulings heal people.
TABRISI:16:69-70/r5.anchor: وروي عن مجاهد أن الهاء في فيه راجعة إلى القرآن أي القرآن فيه شفاء للناس

TABRISI:16:69-70/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:16:69-70/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:16:69-70/r6.claim: Most commentators take the pronoun to mean honey, and this is stronger because the Qur’an had not been mentioned before the pronoun.
TABRISI:16:69-70/r6.anchor: والأول قول أكثر المفسرين وهو الأقوى إذا لم يسبق للقرآن ذكر

TABRISI:16:69-70/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:16:69-70/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:16:69-70/r7.claim: The bee offers several signs: honey comes from its mouth, healing comes from the source of its sting, and its construction and nature contain wonders.
TABRISI:16:69-70/r7.anchor: وفي النحل والعسل وجوه من الاعتبار منها اختصاصه بخروج العسل من فيه ومنها جعل الشفاء من موضع السم

TABRISI:16:69-70/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:16:69-70/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:16:69-70/r8.claim: Each bee group has a leader that protects, directs, and governs it; the followers track it, and the group’s order collapses if it is lost.
TABRISI:16:69-70/r8.anchor: ومن أعجبها أن جعل سبحانه لك فئة يعسوبا

TABRISI:16:69-70/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:16:69-70/r9.speaker: أمير المؤمنين ع
TABRISI:16:69-70/r9.claim: The author connects the bee’s leader to ʿAlī’s saying, ‘I am the leader of the believers.’
TABRISI:16:69-70/r9.anchor: وإلى هذا المعنى فيما قال أشار أمير المؤمنين ع في قوله أنا يعسوب المؤمنين

THALABI:v6p27/r11.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p27/r11.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p27/r11.claim: From every fruit is not universal, as in other verses that say a person received everything or a wind destroyed everything.
THALABI:v6p27/r11.anchor: ثم كلي من كل الثمرات ليس معنى الكل العموم

THALABI:v6p27/r12.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p27/r12.speaker: مجاهد
THALABI:v6p27/r12.claim: Some say ذللا describes the bee's routes as made easy; Mujahid says no place it travels is rugged.

THALABI:v6p27/r13.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p27/r13.speaker: قتادة
THALABI:v6p27/r13.claim: Others, including Qatada, take ذللا as describing the bees themselves: obedient and compliant.
THALABI:v6p27/r13.anchor: قال قتادة وغيره: يعني مطيعة منقادة

THALABI:v6p27/r14.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p27/r14.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p27/r14.claim: The bees' drink emerges in differing colors and contains healing for people.
THALABI:v6p27/r14.anchor: يخرج من بطونها شراب مختلف ألوانه أبيض وأحمر وأصفر فيه شفاء للناس

THALABI:v6p27/r15.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p27/r15.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
THALABI:v6p27/r15.claim: A report from Abu Said says the Prophet repeatedly told a man with an ill brother to give him honey; after another dose, the brother recovered.
THALABI:v6p27/r15.anchor: يروى أن رجلا أتى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال: إن أخي يشتكي بطنه

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:16:69-70/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:16:69-70/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:16:69-70/r1.claim: Bees follow their Lord's paths docilely and obediently while foraging; their honey differs in color, and it heals ailments that honey can cure.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:16:69-70/r1.anchor: منقادة مسخرة مطيعة { يخرج من بطونها شراب

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p73/r4.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p73/r4.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p73/r4.claim: The bee follows the paths its Lord has laid out for it and produces honey, a healing medicine for people.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p73/r4.anchor: طرق ربك التي جعل الله لك.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p73/r5.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p73/r5.speaker: قتادة
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p73/r5.claim: Qatāda glosses the bee's paths as docile, meaning the bee itself is obedient.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p73/r6.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p73/r6.speaker: مجاهد
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p73/r6.claim: Mujāhid says the paths are made easy for the bee, with no place too difficult or rugged to traverse.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p73/r6.anchor: وقال مجاهد: {فاسلكي سبل ربك ذللا} [النحل: 69] ، ذللت لها السبل لا يتوعر عليها مكان.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p73/r7.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p73/r7.speaker: رسول الله
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p73/r7.claim: A man reported his brother's stomach ailment; after repeated instructions to give honey, the brother recovered, and the Prophet said God's word was true and the brother's stomach had lied.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p73/r7.anchor: فقال رسول الله صلى الله عليه في الثالثة أو في الرابعة: «صدق الله وكذب بطن أخيك، اذهب فاسقه عسلا، فذهب فسقاه فبرأ بإذن الله»

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p74/r1.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p74/r1.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p74/r1.claim: The sign in the bee is like the preceding signs.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p74/r1.anchor: قوله: {إن في ذلك لآية لقوم يتفكرون} [النحل: 69] هي مثل الأولى.

ASAD-NOTES:16:68#n78/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:16:68#n78/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:16:68#n78/r1.claim: Asad notes that the phrase literally means "thy Sustainer's paths".

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:16:68/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:16:68/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:16:68/r4.claim: Bees collect nectar, the raw material of honey, and flower pollen as nourishing products, using them for themselves and to make honey and beeswax.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:16:68/r4.anchor: “her türlü besleyici ürünler”den nektar denilen bal ham maddesi ve çiçek tozu toplayarak bunları hem kendi tüketimi için hem de bal ve bal mumu yapmak için değerlendirmektedir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:16:68/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:16:68/r5.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:16:68/r5.claim: Bees contribute more to pollinating fruits, vegetables, and crops than all other insects together.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:16:68/r5.anchor: meyve, sebze ve ekinlerde tozlaşmayı sağlama konusunda da bütün diğer böceklerin toplamından daha fazla iş görmektedir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:16:68/r6.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:16:68/r6.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:16:68/r6.claim: It is notable that the bee’s product is called sharāb, or a drink/syrup, in the verse.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:16:68/r6.anchor: Âyette arının ürettiği madde için “şerâb” (şerbet) kelimesinin kullanılması ilgi çekicidir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:16:68/r7.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:16:68/r7.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:16:68/r7.claim: A bee carries nectar in a specially created honey stomach separate from its ordinary stomach; a young bee then sucks it through its proboscis, transfers it to its own stomach, and processes it to syrup consistency.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:16:68/r7.anchor: Arı topladığı nektarı, normal midesinden ayrı, özel olarak bu maksatla yaratılmış bulunan bal midesine toplayıp kovana taşımakta; burada bir genç arı bu maddeyi hortumuyla emip kendi midesine aktarmakta ve onu şerbet kıvamına gelecek şekilde işleme tâbi tutmaktadır.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:16:68/r8.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:16:68/r8.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:16:68/r8.claim: After honey forms, the syrup is aired in the comb until it solidifies, then sealed with beeswax to prevent spoilage.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:16:68/r8.anchor: bundan sonra şerbet peteklerde bir süre havalandırılarak katılaşması sağlandıktan sonra, üzeri bal mumuyla kapatılıp izole edilmek suretiyle bozulması önlenir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:16:68/r9.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:16:68/r9.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:16:68/r9.claim: By God’s grace this process produces another food that nourishes people and also has healing value.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:16:68/r9.anchor: Böylece Allah’ın lutuf ve ihsanıyla insanlar için besleyiciliği yanında şifa değeri de taşıyan yeni bir besin daha ortaya çıkmış olur.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:16:68/r10.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:16:68/r10.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:16:68/r10.claim: The bee’s extraordinary workmanship cannot be explained without accounting for God’s creative power and wisdom.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:16:68/r10.anchor: Bütün bunlar olağan üstü bir sanat kabiliyetinin tezahürü olup Allah’ın yaratıcı kudretini ve hikmetini hesaba katmadan, basit bir hayvanın böyle bir eseri ve ürünü nasıl meydana getirebildiği sorusunu cevaplandırmak mümkün değildir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:16:68/r11.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:16:68/r11.speaker: bazı mutasavvıflar
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:16:68/r11.claim: Some Sufis hold that reaching sainthood requires accepting afflictions and that a saint may not be treated medically.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:16:68/r11.anchor: bazı mutasavvıfların, “Velîlik makamına ulaşmak için belâlara razı olmak gerekir, velîye tedavi câiz değildir” şeklindeki fikrini

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:16:68/r12.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:16:68/r12.speaker: Kurtubî
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:16:68/r12.claim: Kurtubi argues that the verse’s statement that honey heals people refutes the Sufi claim that a saint may not receive treatment.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:16:68/r12.anchor: Kurtubî’ye göre âyetin “Onda (balda) insanlara şifa var” meâlindeki kısmı, bazı mutasavvıfların

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:16:68/r13.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:16:68/r13.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:16:68/r13.claim: Some hadiths are also reported concerning honey’s healing effects; the commentary refers readers to Ibn Kathir and al-Shawkani without giving a grading here.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:16:68/r13.anchor: Balın şifalı olduğuna dair bazı hadisler de rivayet edilmiştir (bk. İbn Kesîr, IV, 501-503; Şevkânî, III, 200);

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:16:68/r14.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:16:68/r14.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:16:68/r14.claim: Modern medicine also recognizes honey’s healing and protective properties, linked to its sucrose, fructose, protein, acids, and organic and mineral substances.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:16:68/r14.anchor: modern tıpta da bileşimindeki sakaroz, friktoz, protein, asit, organik ve madenî maddeler dolayısıyla balın hem şifa verici hem de koruyucu bir özelliğe sahip olduğu kabul edilmektedir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:16:68/r15.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:16:68/r15.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:16:68/r15.claim: The authors’ rendering of the bee’s path as following its Lord’s laws highlights the varied and remarkable routes bees take in flight.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:16:68/r15.anchor: “Rabbinin koyduğu kanunlara boyun eğerek çizdiği yollardan git!” şeklinde çevirdiğimiz cümle, arıların uçuşlarında izlediği yolların da farklılığına ve ilginçliğine dikkat çekmektedir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:16:68/r16.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:16:68/r16.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:16:68/r16.claim: A 1940s observation says bees usually orient themselves by the sun, and also use the wind’s direction and the earth’s magnetic field.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:16:68/r16.anchor: 1940’larda yapılan bir tesbite göre arılar, genellikle güneşin konumundan yararlanarak yönlerini ayarlamakta; ayrıca rüzgârın yönü, dünyanın manyetik alanı gibi başka imkânlardan da yararlanmaktadır.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:16:68/r17.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:16:68/r17.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:16:68/r17.claim: Bees signal directions and flower locations by circling or drawing an eight over the hive; informed bees find unfamiliar flower areas and return by the shortest route, called the bee line.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:16:68/r17.anchor: Arıların, kovan üzerinde daire veya 8 çizerek birbirlerine yol tarif ettikleri, çiçek alanları hakkında bilgi aktardıkları, bu bilgileri alan diğer arıların, bilmedikleri çiçek alanlarını kolaylıkla buldukları, dönüşlerinde ise “arı hattı” denilen en kestirme yolu kullandıkları da bilinmektedir.

BURSEVI:v5p39/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p39/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p39/r3.claim: The sequence after the bee’s rest turns to eating, and thumma signals the marvel and ease with which this broadly available food is provided.
BURSEVI:v5p39/r3.anchor: ولما كان عاما في كل ثمر ذكره بحرف التراخي إشارة إلى عجيب الصنع في ذلك وتيسره لها

BURSEVI:v5p39/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p39/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p39/r4.claim: من كل الثمرات can signal abundant provision, by analogy with Solomon being given everything.
BURSEVI:v5p39/r4.anchor: فهو للتكثير كقوله تعالى : {وأوتيت من كل شىء}

BURSEVI:v5p39/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p39/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p39/r5.claim: Alternatively, it means all fruits the bee desires, sweet, sour, bitter, and otherwise, with the general wording qualified by ordinary usage.
BURSEVI:v5p39/r5.anchor: أو من كل الثمرات المشتهاة عندك من حلوها وحامضها ومرها وغير ذلك فهو عام مخصوص بالعادة

BURSEVI:v5p39/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p39/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p39/r6.claim: The command to follow the paths answers an implicit condition: after eating fruits far from home, the bee enters the way back to its hive.
BURSEVI:v5p39/r6.anchor: فإذا أكلت الثمار في المواضع البعيدة من بيوتك فادخلي

BURSEVI:v5p39#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p39#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p39#2/r1.claim: The bee’s paths through mountains and trees are routes God taught it for returning to its hive; ذللا means made easy and passable.
BURSEVI:v5p39#2/r1.anchor: طرق ربك التي ألهمك وعرفك الرجوع فيها إلى مكانك من الخلية بعد بعدك عنها

BURSEVI:v5p39#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p39#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p39#2/r2.claim: When nearby forage is exhausted, bees travel to distant pastures and return home without confusion or deviation.
BURSEVI:v5p39#2/r2.anchor: إذا أجدب عليها ما حولها سافرت إلى المواضع البعيدة في طلب النجعة ثم ترجع إلى بيوتها من غير التباس وانحراف

BURSEVI:v5p39#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p39#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p39#2/r3.claim: Calling these routes the Lord’s points to God’s great care: without it the bee would not know how to find its way.
BURSEVI:v5p39#2/r3.anchor: وأشار باسم الرب إلى أنه لولا عظيم إحسانه في تربيتها لما اهتدت إلى ذلك

BURSEVI:v5p39#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p39#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p39#2/r4.claim: The bee’s navigation is compared with the quṭā bird, which travels far for water and returns accurately between dawn and sunrise.
BURSEVI:v5p39#2/r4.anchor: وذلك أنه يترك فراخه ثم يطلب الماء من مسيرة عشرة أيام وأكثر

BURSEVI:v5p39#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p39#2/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p39#2/r5.claim: The drink is honey, produced when bees eat fine sweet substances on leaves and flowers, suck wet fruits and fragrant things, then regurgitate and store them for winter until honey forms by God’s leave.
BURSEVI:v5p39#2/r5.anchor: وإلى هذا أشار ظهير الفاريابي بقوله :

BURSEVI:v5p39#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p39#2/r6.speaker: ظهير الفاريابي
BURSEVI:v5p39#2/r6.claim: Ẓahīr al-Fāriyābī’s Persian verse depicts the bee waiting in greedy desire to sweeten the mouth before vomiting honey.
BURSEVI:v5p39#2/r6.anchor: أشار ظهير الفاريابي بقوله : بدان طمع كه دهن خوش كنى زغايت حرص

BURSEVI:v5p39#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p39#2/r7.speaker: علي رضي الله عنه
BURSEVI:v5p39#2/r7.claim: ʿAlī belittles worldly honors by calling humanity a worm’s saliva and honey a bee’s excretion; Bursevī says the disparaging wording concerns appearance, since honey itself is delicious.
BURSEVI:v5p39#2/r7.anchor: وأما قول علي رضي الله عنه في تحقير الدنيا أشرف الناس ابن آدم فيها لعاب دودة

BURSEVI:v5p39#2/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p39#2/r8.speaker: حياة الحيوان
BURSEVI:v5p39#2/r8.claim: A discussion of the bee’s poison, honey, and wax presents their coexistence as proof of divine power and compares the believer’s work, mixed with fear and hope.
BURSEVI:v5p39#2/r8.anchor: قد جمع الله تعالى في النحلة السم والعسل دليلا على كمال قدرته وأخرج منها العسل ممزوجا بالشمع وكذلك عمل المؤمن ممزوج بالخوف والرجاء

BURSEVI:v5p39#3/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p39#3/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p39#3/r1.claim: Honey is called al-Ḥāfiẓ al-Amīn because it preserves the dead indefinitely, meat for three months, fruit for six months, and other perishable things much longer.
BURSEVI:v5p39#3/r1.anchor: منها الحافظ الأمين لأنه يحفظ ما يودع فيه فيحفظ الميت أبدا واللحم ثلاثة أشهر والفاكهة ستة أشهر

BURSEVI:v5p39#3/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p39#3/r2.speaker: النبي عليه السلام
BURSEVI:v5p39#3/r2.claim: The Prophet liked sweets and honey; scholars explain “sweets” broadly and the later mention of honey as singling out its special merit.
BURSEVI:v5p39#3/r2.anchor: وكان عليه السلام يحب الحلواء والعسل.

BURSEVI:v5p39#3/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p39#3/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p39#3/r3.claim: Eating delicious foods and good provisions is permissible and does not contradict asceticism or watchfulness, especially when accompanied by spending in charity.
BURSEVI:v5p39#3/r3.anchor: وفيه جواز أكل لذيذ الأطعمة والطيبات من الرزق وأن ذلك لا ينافي الزهد والمراقبة لا سيما إذا حصل إنفاق

BURSEVI:v5p39#3/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p39#3/r4.speaker: النبي عليه السلام
BURSEVI:v5p39#3/r4.claim: A prophetic report says honey is the first blessing to be removed from the earth.

BURSEVI:v5p39#3/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p39#3/r5.speaker: علي رضي الله عنه
BURSEVI:v5p39#3/r5.claim: ʿAlī lists six worldly things and their finest examples: honey, water, silk, a horse, musk, and a woman, each paired with an earthy or troubling source or consequence.
BURSEVI:v5p39#3/r5.anchor: وقال علي رضي الله عنه : إنما الدنيا ستة أشياء : مطعوم ومشروب وملبوس

BURSEVI:v5p39#3/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p39#3/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p39#3/r6.claim: Honey’s colors include white, yellow, and red, attributed either to the bees’ life stages or to differences in the flowers’ colors.
BURSEVI:v5p39#3/r6.anchor: من أبيض وأخضر وأصفر وأسود بسبب اختلاف سن النحل

BURSEVI:v5p39#3/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p39#3/r7.speaker: حكيم يونان
BURSEVI:v5p39#3/r7.claim: A Greek sage tells students to imitate bees: idle bees are expelled because they crowd the hive and consume honey, while only the active work.
BURSEVI:v5p39#3/r7.anchor: قال حكيم يونان لتلامذته كونوا كالنحل في الخلايا وهي بيوتها

BURSEVI:v5p39#3/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p39#3/r8.speaker: ابن عمر رضي الله عنهما
BURSEVI:v5p39#3/r8.claim: Ibn ʿUmar compares the believer to a bee: it eats and produces good things, is perceptive and useful, causes little harm, avoids filth, and obeys God.
BURSEVI:v5p39#3/r8.anchor: وعن ابن عمر رضي الله عنهما مثل المؤمن كالنحلة تأكل طيبا وتصنع طيبا ووجه المشابهة بينهما حذق النحل وفطنته وقلة أذاه

BURSEVI:v5p39#3/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p39#3/r9.speaker: ابن عمر رضي الله عنهما
BURSEVI:v5p39#3/r9.claim: Bee hazards—darkness, clouds, wind, smoke, water, and fire—are likened to the believer’s spiritual hazards: heedlessness, doubt, temptation, unlawful things, folly, and ardent longing.
BURSEVI:v5p39#3/r9.anchor: وأن للنحل آفات تقطعه عن عمله منها الظلمة والغيم والريح والدخان والماء والنار وكذلك المؤمن له آفات تغيره عن عمله

BURSEVI:v5p39#3/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p39#3/r10.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p39#3/r10.claim: The honey’s healing applies to ailments known to respond to it; the verse does not promise a cure for every disease or every person.
BURSEVI:v5p39#3/r10.anchor: لا يقتضي العموم لكل علة وفي كل إنسان لأنه نكرة في سياق الإثبات

BURSEVI:v5p39#3/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p39#3/r11.speaker: ابن مسعود وابن عمر رضي الله عنهم
BURSEVI:v5p39#3/r11.claim: Ibn Masʿūd and Ibn ʿUmar are reported to understand the phrase “healing for people” generally.
BURSEVI:v5p39#3/r11.anchor: وكان ابن مسعود وابن عمر رضي الله عنهم يحملانه على العموم

BURSEVI:v5p40/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p40/r1.speaker: البيضاوي
BURSEVI:v5p40/r1.claim: Al-Bayḍāwī says honey heals directly in phlegmatic illnesses and as an ingredient in other medicines; sugar was regionally limited and was not used in earlier remedies as honey was.
BURSEVI:v5p40/r1.anchor: قال البيضاوي : {فيه شفآء للناس} إما بنفسه كما في الأمراض البلغمية

BURSEVI:v5p40/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p40/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BURSEVI:v5p40/r2.claim: A man repeatedly gives honey to his brother for a stomach complaint; early doses worsen diarrhea, but the final dose cures him, and the Prophet says God told the truth while the stomach lied.
BURSEVI:v5p40/r2.anchor: فعاد إلى النبي عليه الصلاة والسلام فذكر له ذلك فقال : "اسقه عسلا"

BURSEVI:v5p40/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p40/r3.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BURSEVI:v5p40/r3.claim: A prophetic report names black seed, cupping, honey, and rainwater as four sources of healing.
BURSEVI:v5p40/r3.anchor: وفي الحديث "إن الله جعل الشفاء في أربعة الحبة السوداء والحجامة والعسل وماء السماء"

BURSEVI:v5p40/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p40/r4.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
BURSEVI:v5p40/r4.claim: ʿAlī recommends a memory remedy: obtain two dirhams from one’s wife’s dowry with her consent, buy milk and honey, mix them with rainwater, and drink before eating.
BURSEVI:v5p40/r4.anchor: علي بن أبي طالب كرم الله وجهه وشكا له سوء الحفظ فقال : أترجع إلى أهل

BURSEVI:v5p40/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p40/r5.speaker: الحسن بن الفضل
BURSEVI:v5p40/r5.claim: Al-Ḥasan ibn al-Faḍl traces the remedy to verses describing blessed rain, pure and pleasant milk, healing honey, and a wholesome bridal gift; their combined qualities explain its benefit.
BURSEVI:v5p40/r5.anchor: فسئل الحسن بن الفضل عن هذا فقال : أخذه من قوله تعالى :

BURSEVI:v5p40/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p40/r6.speaker: الحسن بن الفضل
BURSEVI:v5p40/r6.claim: The milk, honey, and dowry portions of the remedy are supported by verses on pure milk, honey’s healing, and a wholesome gift.
BURSEVI:v5p40/r6.anchor: فسئل الحسن بن الفضل عن هذا فقال : أخذه من قوله تعالى : {ونزلنا من السمآء مآء مباركا} (ق : 9) وفي اللبن {خالصا سآااغا للشاربين}

BURSEVI:v5p40/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p40/r7.speaker: عوف بن مالك
BURSEVI:v5p40/r7.claim: When ill, ʿAwf ibn Mālik combines rainwater, honey, and blessed olive oil, citing verses about each, and is cured.
BURSEVI:v5p40/r7.anchor: وروي عن عوف بن مالك أنه مرض فقال : ائتوني بماء فإن الله تعالى قال :

BURSEVI:v5p40/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p40/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p40/r8.claim: Some people use honey as an eye treatment and for illnesses; unmixed honey with musk is said to help cataracts, while smearing honey kills lice.
BURSEVI:v5p40/r8.anchor: وكان بعضهم يكتحل بالعسل ويتداوى به من كل سقم وإذا خلط العسل الذي لم يصبه ماء ولا نار ولا دخان بشيء من المسك

BURSEVI:v5p41#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p41#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p41#2/r1.claim: The bee’s honey-making is a manifest proof of divine power: a small, weak creature cannot devise the craft on its own, so it points to one capable Creator without partner or likeness.
BURSEVI:v5p41#2/r1.anchor: حجة ظاهرة دالة على القدرة الربانية

BURSEVI:v5p41#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p41#2/r2.speaker: الكاشفي
BURSEVI:v5p41#2/r2.claim: Kāshifī says reflection on the bee’s delicate crafts and obedient, long-distance navigation shows that a powerful, knowing God inspires wisdom into a weak creature.
BURSEVI:v5p41#2/r2.anchor: قال الكاشفي : {لقوم يتفكرون} (مركر وهى راكه تفكر كنند

BURSEVI:v5p41#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p41#2/r3.speaker: الكاشفي
BURSEVI:v5p41#2/r3.claim: Kāshifī reads the bee’s bitter diet and sweet honey, cleanliness, exact return home, and hexagonal engineering as signs that reflection cures inward ignorance just as honey treats outward illness.
BURSEVI:v5p41#2/r3.anchor: خورند وعسل شيرين بازدهند ورعى كه جز اك واكيزه نخورند طاعتى كه هركز خلاف فرمان نكنند

BURSEVI:v5p41#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p41#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p41#2/r4.claim: The Persian verses compare reflective thought to honey: when its sweetness reaches the soul, its trace remains forever.
BURSEVI:v5p41#2/r4.anchor: فكر دلرانيك وهم نمكين كند كام جانرا ون عسل شيرين كند

BURSEVI:v5p41#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p41#2/r5.speaker: القشيري
BURSEVI:v5p41#2/r5.claim: Al-Qushayrī says God hides precious things in humble places—silk in worms, honey in bees, pearls in shells, and precious metals in stone—and likewise places knowledge and love in imperfect believers.
BURSEVI:v5p41#2/r5.anchor: قال القشيري رحمه الله : إن الله تعالى أجرى سنته أن يخفي كل عزيز في شيء حقير

BURSEVI:v5p41#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p41#2/r6.speaker: القشيري
BURSEVI:v5p41#2/r6.claim: Al-Qushayrī’s verse cautions that someone who seems insignificant may in fact possess spiritual sainthood.
BURSEVI:v5p41#2/r6.anchor: كسى راكه نزديك ظنت بداوست ندانى كه صاحب ولايت هم اوست

BURSEVI:v5p41#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p41#2/r7.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v5p41#2/r7.claim: The Najmī commentary says every animal’s varied actions arise from God’s instruction and inspiration under His wisdom and eternal will, rather than from its nature or desire.
BURSEVI:v5p41#2/r7.anchor: قال في "التأويلات النجمية" : في الآية إشارة إلى أن تصرف كل حيوان

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Elsewhere the sequence of hearing, understanding, and reflection ascends: at minimum a sane person should listen to sensible speech and try to understand it; one who cannot is like an animal on two legs.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: This, on the other hand, is an ascending order sequence.

ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p357#6/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p357#6/r1.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p357#6/r1.claim: Qatadah glosses the bees’ paths as obedient or submissive.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p357#6/r1.anchor: عن معمر عن قتادة في قوله تعالى ﴿ ذللا ﴾ قال مطيعة

ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p357#6/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p357#6/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p357#6/r2.claim: The Prophet directs a man whose brother has abdominal illness to give honey; after a second dose, the illness resolves, confirming honey’s healing.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p357#6/r2.anchor: فقال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم اذهب فاسق أخاك عسلا فقد صدق الله وكذب بطن أخيك فسقى له فكأنما نشط من عقال فبرأ

ALUSI-FULL:v14p182#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p182#2/r1.speaker: ابن عطية
ALUSI-FULL:v14p182#2/r1.claim: Ibn Atiyya reads all fruits literally as tree produce and says bees eat blossoms; fruit can also name the tree itself.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p182#2/r1.anchor: وأخذ بظاهر ذلك ابن عطية فقال : إنما تأكل النوار من الأشجار وتقال الثمرة للشجرة أيضا كما في القاموس

ALUSI-FULL:v14p182#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p182#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v14p182#2/r2.claim: A broader reading, more suitable here, takes fruit as the plant because bees also eat leaves and flowers; the author objects that fruit meaning tree is an unfamiliar metaphor and eating other matter is unproven.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p182#2/r2.anchor: وقيل : وهو المناسب هنا إذا التخصيص بحمل الشجر خلاف الواقع لعموم أكلها للأوراق والأزهار والثمار

ALUSI-FULL:v14p182#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p182#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v14p182#2/r3.claim: The phrase all fruits can mean every kind bees customarily desire; some take all as intensive, and al-Khafaji says even a literal universal is possible because the command grants permission rather than requiring eating all of them. Min remains partitive.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p182#2/r3.anchor: وجوز أن يكون نخصوصا بالعادة أي كلي من كل ثمرة تشتهينها وقيل : ( كل ) للتكثير قال الخفاجي

ALUSI-FULL:v14p183/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p183/r1.speaker: الإمام
ALUSI-FULL:v14p183/r1.claim: The Imam describes two accounts: bees collect a subtle dew-like substance from flowers and leaves and store it as honey, or eat fragrant plant matter that God transforms inside them before they regurgitate honey.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p183/r1.anchor: فقد تكون تلم الأجزاء لطيفة صغيرة متفرقة على الأوراق والأزهار وقد تكون كثيرة بحيث بجتمع منها

ALUSI-FULL:v14p183/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p183/r2.speaker: الإمام
ALUSI-FULL:v14p183/r2.claim: The Imam favors the collected-dew account as more rational and consistent with observation, comparing the substance to taranjabin, which falls from the air and gathers on plants.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p183/r2.anchor: والقول الأول أقرب إلى العقل وأشد مناسبة للاستقراء فإن طبيعة الترنجبين قربية من العسل في الطعم والشكل

ALUSI-FULL:v14p183/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p183/r3.speaker: الإمام
ALUSI-FULL:v14p183/r3.claim: The Imam argues that observing bees eat honey and leaving them a remainder after harvesting supports the view that they collect food and store it.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p183/r3.anchor: وأيضا فنحن نشاهد أن النحل تتغذى بالعسل حتى إذا أخرجنا العسل من بيوتها تركنا لها بقية منه لغذائها

ALUSI-FULL:v14p183/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p183/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v14p183/r4.claim: The author says the apparent command to eat favors the second account more strongly than taranjabin's resemblance favors the first; honey and taranjabin also have distinct medical temperaments.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p183/r4.anchor: وأنت تعلم أن ظاهر ( كلي ) يؤيد القول الثاني وهو أشد تأييدا له من تأييد مشابهة الترنجبين للعسل

ALUSI-FULL:v14p183/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p183/r5.speaker: بعض أجلة الأطباء
ALUSI-FULL:v14p183/r5.claim: Some eminent physicians classify honey as hot in the third degree and dry in the second, but taranjabin as hot in the first and moist in the second or balanced.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p183/r5.anchor: فقد ذكر بعض أجلة الأطباء أن العسل حار في الثالثة يابس في الثانية والترنجبين حار في الأولى رطب في الثانية

ALUSI-FULL:v14p183/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p183/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v14p183/r6.claim: The author explains that taranjabin is Persian for damp honey from dew, but notes it is actually dew on camel thorn in Persia; an imported substance called tanit resembles it in appearance and effect but is thicker.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p183/r6.anchor: فإن ترنجبين فارسي معناه عسل رطب لاطل الندا كما زعم وإن قالوا : هو في الحقيقة طل يسقط على العاقول بفارس

ALUSI-FULL:v14p183/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p183/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v14p183/r7.claim: Seeing bees feed on honey is not decisive because this is not constant; reports about birds eating their own droppings similarly weaken that inference.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p183/r7.anchor: والأمر في مشاهدة تغذيها بالعسل سهل فإنه ليس دائميا وينقل عن الطيور التي تمكن شتاء التغذي بالرجيع

ALUSI-FULL:v14p183/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p183/r8.speaker: علي
ALUSI-FULL:v14p183/r8.claim: Ali is quoted as belittling worldly honor: humanity's finest clothing is a worm's saliva and finest drink is bees' regurgitation; he also calls honey a fly's vomit.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p183/r8.anchor: ويؤيد المشهور ما روي عن الأمير علي كرم الله تعالى وجهه في تحقير الدنيا أشرف لباس ابن آدم فيها لعاب دودة وأشرف شرابه رجيع نحل

ALUSI-FULL:v14p183/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p183/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v14p183/r9.claim: The author says taking the report literally is the apparent reading, and cites al-Maʿarri's verse about bees making honey from bitter flowers and al-Hariri's contrast between bees and wasps.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p183/r9.anchor: وحمله على التمثيل خلاف الظاهر وعلى ذلك نظمت الأشعار فقال المعري : والنحل يجني المر من زهر الربا

ALUSI-FULL:v14p183/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p183/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v14p183/r10.claim: A trusted observer saw bees carrying flower leaves to their nests in their mouths, which supports their eating plant matter; further evidence is promised later.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p183/r10.anchor: وأخبرني من أثق به أنه شاهد كثيرا حملها لأوراق الأزهار بفمها إلى بيوتها وهو مما يستأنس به للأكل

ALUSI-FULL:v14p183/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p183/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v14p183/r11.claim: The bee is told to follow its Lord's paths back to its nest after feeding; when nearby forage runs out it travels far yet returns without losing its way, and the possessive wording signals divine preparation and care.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p183/r11.anchor: أي طرقه سبحانه راجعة إلى بيوتك بعد الأكل فالمراد بالسبل مسالكها في العود

ALUSI-FULL:v14p183/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p183/r12.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v14p183/r12.claim: Another view takes the paths as routes to food sources, making eat mean seek food; another makes them the inspired methods of producing honey.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p183/r12.anchor: وقيل : المراد من السبل طرق الذهاب إلى مظان ما تأكل منه وحينئذ فمعنى ( كلي ) اقصدي الأكل

ALUSI-FULL:v14p183/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p183/r13.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v14p183/r13.claim: A further metaphor makes the paths routes by which food is transformed into honey: salk is transitive, as in threading a string through a needle, with the object omitted.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p183/r13.anchor: وقيل : السبل مجاز عن طرق العمل وأنواعها أي فاسلكي الطرق التي ألهمك ربك في عمل العسل

ALUSI-FULL:v14p183/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p183/r14.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v14p183/r14.claim: The command is not necessarily problematic because entering the passageways is voluntary even if the resulting transformation is not; the author rejects the objection that the whole process is involuntary.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p183/r14.anchor: ورد بأنه ليس بشيء لأن الإدخال باختيارها فلا يضره كون الإحالة المترتبة عليه ليست اختيارية

ALUSI-FULL:v14p183/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p183/r15.speaker: مجاهد
ALUSI-FULL:v14p183/r15.claim: Mujahid explains dhululan as paths made tame and easy by God; it is the plural of dhalul and describes the paths.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p183/r15.anchor: أي مذللة ذللها الله تعالى وسهلها لك فهو جمع ذلول حال من السبل وروي هذا عن مجاهد

ALUSI-FULL:v14p183/r16.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p183/r16.speaker: قتادة
ALUSI-FULL:v14p183/r16.claim: Qatada instead takes dhululan as obedient and compliant, describing the bee itself.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p183/r16.anchor: وقال قتادة : أي مطيعة منقادة فهو حال من الضمير في ( فاسلكي )

ALUSI-FULL:v14p183/r17.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p183/r17.speaker: ابن عبد السلام
ALUSI-FULL:v14p183/r17.claim: Ibn Abd al-Salam argues that the paths must be food passages rather than travel routes because the air is not a beaten, trodden path; the author finds this reasoning questionable.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p183/r17.anchor: وجعل ابن عبد السلام وصف السبل بالذلل دليلا على أن المراد بالسبل مسالك الغذاء لا طرق الذهاب

ALUSI-FULL:v14p183/r18.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p183/r18.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v14p183/r18.claim: The phrase about honey coming from their bellies starts a new sentence and shifts from addressing bees to addressing people, who should reflect on the wonders of God's creation.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p183/r18.anchor: استئناف عدل به عن خطاب النحل إلى الكلام مع الناس لبيان ما يظهر منها من تعاجيب صنع الله

ALUSI-FULL:v14p183/r19.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p183/r19.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v14p183/r19.claim: Honey is called a drink because people drink it; Arabic usage says one drank honey rather than ate it.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p183/r19.anchor: شراب ( يعني العسل وسمي بذلك لأنه مما يشرب حتى قيل : إنه لا يقال : أكلت عسلا وإنما يقال : شربت عسلا

ALUSI-FULL:v14p183/r20.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p183/r20.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v14p183/r20.claim: The verse does not explicitly say that God brings the drink forth, since His earlier attribution of inspiration to Himself suffices; this signals that His intention alone brings the thing about.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p183/r20.anchor: اكتفاءا بإسناد الإيحاء بالمبادي إليه جل شأنه وفيه إيذان بعظيم قدرته عز وجل بحيث أن ما يشعر بإرادة الشيء كاف في حصوله

ALUSI-FULL:v14p184/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p184/r1.speaker: الجمهور
ALUSI-FULL:v14p184/r1.claim: Most commentators say the honey exits the bees’ mouths; some call that account a stronger display of divine power, and al-Ḥarīrī’s verse and al-Ḥasan’s saying support it.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p184/r1.anchor: والجمهور على أنه يخرج من أفواهها وزعم بعضهم أنه أبلغ في القدرة وبيت الحريري على ذلك وكذا قول الحسن

ALUSI-FULL:v14p184/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p184/r2.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v14p184/r2.claim: A minority says honey exits from the bees’ rear, citing what they take as an apparent report from ʿAlī, called the Commander of the Believers.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p184/r2.anchor: وقيل : من أدبارها وهو ظاهر ما روي عن يعسوب المؤمنين كرم الله تعالى وجهه

ALUSI-FULL:v14p184/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p184/r3.speaker: آخرون
ALUSI-FULL:v14p184/r3.claim: Others decline to specify the honey’s exit beyond what the verse itself states.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p184/r3.anchor: وقال آخرون : لا ندري إلا ما ذكره الله تعالى

ALUSI-FULL:v14p184/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p184/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v14p184/r4.claim: A story says Solomon, Alexander, and Aristotle built glass hives to observe how bees make honey, but the bees covered the glass interior with clay and prevented inspection.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p184/r4.anchor: وحكى أن سليمان عليه السلام والإسكندر وأرسطو صنعوا لها بيوتا من زجاج لينظروا إلى كيفية صنيعها

ALUSI-FULL:v14p184/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p184/r5.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v14p184/r5.claim: Some interpret “bellies” as mouths, since the mouth functions like a belly and is an interior part; this fits their theory that bees gather tiny dew particles and store them as honey.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p184/r5.anchor: وقال بعضهم : المراد بالبطون الأفواه وسمي الفم بطنا لأنه في حكمه ولأنه مما يبطن ولا يظهر

ALUSI-FULL:v14p184/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p184/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v14p184/r6.claim: Al-Ālūsī takes “bellies” in its ordinary sense as the known organ, which supports the widely accepted account that honey forms inside the bee.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p184/r6.anchor: وأنت تعلم أن الظاهر من البطن الجارحة المعروفة فالآية تؤيد القول المشهور في تكون العسل

ALUSI-FULL:v14p184/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p184/r7.speaker: المحققون من الحكماء
ALUSI-FULL:v14p184/r7.claim: Al-Kashf says the command to eat indicates that the bee’s stomach contributes to producing honey; discerning philosophers prefer this account.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p184/r7.anchor: وفي الكشف أن في قوله تعالى : ( ثم كلي ) إشارة إلى أن لمعدة النحل في ذلك تأثيرا وهو المختار عند المحققين من الحكماء

ALUSI-FULL:v14p184/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p184/r8.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v14p184/r8.claim: Those who say honey is wholly plant-derived and “bellies” means mouths must explain “eat”; interpreting eating as merely gathering is, in al-Ālūsī’s view, an unpersuasive reply.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p184/r8.anchor: ومن جعل العسل نباتيا محضا وفسر البطون بأفواه النحل فليت شعري ماذا يصنع بقوله سبحانه : ( ثم كلي )

ALUSI-FULL:v14p184/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p184/r9.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v14p184/r9.claim: Some say bees gather both flowers and dew: what they gather from flowers is honey, while dew yields poison; reason permits reversing this, which may be more plausible.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p184/r9.anchor: ومن الناس من زعم أنها تجتني زهرا وطلا فالمجتني من الزهر نفسه يكون عسلا والمجتني نت الطل يكون موما والعقل يجوز العكس ولعله أقرب من ذلك

ALUSI-FULL:v14p184/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p184/r10.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v14p184/r10.claim: Reported explanations for honey’s white, yellow, red, and black colors include God’s direct will, different forage, different seasons, and the bees’ ages; one account maps the colors from young to very old bees.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p184/r10.anchor: مختلف ألوانه ( بالبياض والصفرة والحمرة والسواد إما لمحض إرادة الصانع الحكيم جل جلاله وإما لاختلاف المرعى أو لاختلاف الفصل أو لاختلاف سن النحل

ALUSI-FULL:v14p184/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p184/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v14p184/r11.claim: Al-Ālūsī says there is no proof for the age-based color theory, but trusted observers found age the strongest apparent cause, supporting the common account of honey forming in bees.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p184/r11.anchor: وتعقب بأنه مما لا دليل عليه وقد سألت جمعا ممن أثق بهم قد اختبروا أحوالها فذكروا أنهم قد استقرؤا وسبروا فرأوا أقوى الأسباب الظاهرة لاختلاف الألوان اختلاف السن

ALUSI-FULL:v14p185/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p185/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v14p185/r1.claim: Honey may heal directly in serious illnesses or work alongside other remedies in less serious ones, and it contributes to many medicinal compounds.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p185/r1.anchor: إما بنفسه كما في الأمراض البليغة أو مع غيره كما في سائر الأمراض إذ يكون معجون لا يكون فيه عسل

ALUSI-FULL:v14p185/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p185/r2.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v14p185/r2.claim: Some object that honey’s presence in medicines may only prevent harm rather than contribute to the cure; al-Ālūsī answers that preserving potency and conveying a medicine’s benefits does aid healing.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p185/r2.anchor: إن دخوله في ذلك لا يقتضي أن يكون له دخل في الشفاء بل عدم الضرر

ALUSI-FULL:v14p185/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p185/r3.speaker: الأطباء
ALUSI-FULL:v14p185/r3.claim: Medical books say honey preserves medicines’ strength for a long time and carries their benefits; al-Ālūsī notes that sugar is not commonly said to replace it in this role.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p185/r3.anchor: ما يحفظ القوي ويبلغ منافع الدواء يصدق عليه أن له دخلا في الشفاء ولم يشتهر أن السكر ينوب منابه في ذلك

ALUSI-FULL:v14p185/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p185/r4.speaker: البحر
ALUSI-FULL:v14p185/r4.claim: Al-Baḥr observes that honey is widely available, whereas sugar was limited to some regions, is a human-made later product, and was not used in earlier medicines and drinks.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p185/r4.anchor: وفي البحر أن العسل موجود كثيرا في أكثر البلاد وأما السكر فمختص به بعض البلاد وهو محدث مصنوع للبشر

ALUSI-FULL:v14p185/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p185/r5.speaker: شرح الشمائل
ALUSI-FULL:v14p185/r5.claim: A statement in Sharḥ al-Shamāʾil says the Prophet never ate sugar.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p185/r5.anchor: وفي شرح الشمائل أنه عليه الصلاة والسلام لم يأكل السكر

ALUSI-FULL:v14p185/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p185/r6.speaker: غير واحد
ALUSI-FULL:v14p185/r6.claim: Several commentators deny that “for people” is universal: honey is unsuitable for some illnesses, including yellow-bile conditions in choleric patients; they distinguish types of oxymel and mean those people whose illnesses benefit from honey.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p185/r6.anchor: وذكر غير واحد أنه ليس بالناس هنا العموم لأن كثيرا من الأمراض لا يدخل في دوائها العسل كأمراض الصفراء فإنه مضر للصفراوي

ALUSI-FULL:v14p185/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p185/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v14p185/r7.claim: The word “healing” can be magnified by the indefinite form or understood partively: honey contains some healing, so it need not cure every illness or every person.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p185/r7.anchor: والتنوين في ( شفاء ) إما للتعظيم أي شفاء ولإما للتبعيض أي فيه بعض الشفاء فلا يقتضي أن كل شفاء به ولا أن كل أحد يستشفى به

ALUSI-FULL:v14p185/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p185/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v14p185/r8.claim: The fact that milk also heals is no objection, since few medicines lack healing in some sense; specifying honey highlights the surprising healing property of a possibly venomous, stinging creature.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p185/r8.anchor: ولا يرد أن اللبن أيضا كذلك بل قلما يوجد شيء من العقاقير إلا وفيه شفاء للناس بهذا المعنى

ALUSI-FULL:v14p185/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p185/r9.speaker: نافع عن ابن عمر
ALUSI-FULL:v14p185/r9.claim: A report says Ibn ʿUmar applied honey to any sore or boil; he defended treating a boil with honey by citing the verse, and al-Ālūsī says physicians confirm its wound-cleansing and healing effects.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p185/r9.anchor: أن ابن عمر رضي الله تعالى عنهما كان لا يشكو قرحة ولا شيئا إلا جعل عليه عسلا حتى الدمل إذا كان به طلاه عسلا

ALUSI-FULL:v14p185/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p185/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v14p185/r10.claim: Al-Ālūsī rejects a universal claim because some illnesses plainly do not benefit from honey; God knows whether reports suggesting universal efficacy are sound.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p185/r10.anchor: والحق أنه لا مساغ للعموم إذ لا شك وجود مرض لا ينفع فيه العسل والآثار المشعرة بالعموم الله تعالى أعلم بصحتها

ALUSI-FULL:v14p185#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p185#2/r1.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
ALUSI-FULL:v14p185#2/r1.claim: A report in Aḥmad, al-Bukhārī, Muslim, and Ibn Mardawayh recounts the Prophet repeatedly prescribing honey for a man’s brother’s diarrhea, after which he recovered.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p185#2/r1.anchor: يا رسول الله إن أخي استطلق بطنه فقال : أسقه عسلا فسقاه عسلا ثم جلم فقال : سقيته عسلا فما زاده إلا استطلاقا

ALUSI-FULL:v14p185#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p185#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v14p185#2/r2.claim: The episode does not prove universal efficacy: God may have informed the Prophet that this particular diarrhea would respond to honey.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p185#2/r2.anchor: فليس صريحا في العموم لجواز أن يكون عليه الصلاة والسلام قد علمه الله سبحانه أن داء هذا المستطلق مما يشفى بالعسل

ALUSI-FULL:v14p185#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p185#2/r3.speaker: طبقات الأطباء
ALUSI-FULL:v14p185#2/r3.claim: A medical explanation says sticky, thick fluids had made the patient’s stomach slippery; honey cleared and expelled them, initially increasing diarrhea until the fluids were exhausted and he recovered.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p185#2/r3.anchor: أنه إنما قال صلى الله عليه وسلم ذلك لأنه علم أن في معدة المريض رطوبات لزجة غليظة قد أزلقت معدته

ALUSI-FULL:v14p185#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p185#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v14p185#2/r4.claim: On the first interpretation, “God is truthful” reflects knowledge God gave His Prophet, while “your brother’s belly lied” metaphorically describes apparent diarrhea that was not a true disease.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p185#2/r4.anchor: فقوله صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم : صدق الله تعالى بالعلم الذي عرف نبيه عليه الصلاة والسلام به وقوله : كذب بطن أخيك يعني ما كان يظهر من بطنه من الإسهال

ALUSI-FULL:v14p185#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p185#2/r5.speaker: الأطباء
ALUSI-FULL:v14p185#2/r5.claim: The medical terminology “false tenesmus” versus “true tenesmus” parallels the description of the brother’s apparent but not genuine disease.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p185#2/r5.anchor: وعلى ذلك قول الأطباء : زحير كاذب وزحير صادق

ALUSI-FULL:v14p185#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p185#2/r6.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v14p185#2/r6.claim: Another interpretation takes “God is truthful” to affirm that honey heals and calls “your brother’s belly lied” an antithetical form of verbal matching.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p185#2/r6.anchor: وقال بعضهم : المراد بصدق الله تعالى صدق سبحانه في أن العسل فيه الشفاء وقوله عليه الصلاة والسلام : كذب بطن أخيك من المشاكلة الضدية

ALUSI-FULL:v14p185#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p185#2/r7.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v14p185#2/r7.claim: One critic rejects antithetical matching as an unfamiliar figure and says the belly seemed to contradict God’s word; al-Ālūsī rejects the criticism as uninformed.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p185#2/r7.anchor: وأنكر بعضهم هذا النوع من من المشاكلة وقال : إنها ليست معروفة وإنه إنما عبر به لأن بطنه كأنه كذب قول الله تعالى بلسان حاله

ALUSI-FULL:v14p185#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p185#2/r8.speaker: يزيد بن يوحنا
ALUSI-FULL:v14p185#2/r8.claim: A parallel case under al-Maʾmūn involved Thumāma al-ʿAbsī, whose severe diarrhea resisted doctors until the physician Yazīd ibn Yūḥannā cured him with a purgative that removed corrupt chyme.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p185#2/r8.anchor: وذلك أن ثمامة العبسي وكان من خواصه مرض بالإسهال فكان يقوم في اليوم والليلة مائة مرة وعجز الأطباء عن علاجه فعالجه يزيد بن يوحنا طبيب الكأمون بالمسهل أيضا فبريء

ALUSI-FULL:v14p185#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p185#2/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v14p185#2/r9.claim: Al-Ālūsī treats the Prophet’s diagnosis as a miracle showing knowledge of subtle medicine without instruction, and says critics who object that honey is a laxative misunderstand medical details.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p185#2/r9.anchor: ومنه يعلم أن ما فعله النبي صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم كان من معجزاته الدالة على علمه بدقائق الطب من غير تعليم

ALUSI-FULL:v14p185#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p185#2/r10.speaker: مجاهد والضحاك والفراء وابن كسيان وابن عباس والحسن
ALUSI-FULL:v14p185#2/r10.claim: These authorities, including one report from Ibn ʿAbbās, take “in it” to refer to the Qurʾān, which heals ignorance and idolatry and provides guidance and mercy.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p185#2/r10.anchor: ونقل عن مجاهد والضحاك والفراء وابن كسيان وهو رواية عن ابن عباس والحسن أن ضمير ( فيه ) للقرآن والمراد أن في القرآن شفاء لأمراض الجهل والشرك

ALUSI-FULL:v14p185#2/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p185#2/r11.speaker: ابن النحاس
ALUSI-FULL:v14p185#2/r11.claim: Ibn al-Naḥḥās approves the interpretation that the pronoun refers to the Qurʾān.

ALUSI-FULL:v14p186/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p186/r1.speaker: القاضي أبو بكر بن العربي
ALUSI-FULL:v14p186/r1.claim: Ibn al-ʿArabī says attributing the Qurʾān interpretation to those scholars is textually and rationally unsound: the context is honey, and the preceding book verse is not a plausible antecedent for them.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p186/r1.anchor: أرى هذا القول لا يصح نقله عن هؤلاء ولو صح نقلا لم يصح عقلا فإن سياق الكلام كله للعسل ليس للقرآن فيه ذكر

ALUSI-FULL:v14p186/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p186/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v14p186/r2.claim: Al-Ālūsī affirms that the Qurʾān is indeed a healing, and cites Ibn Masʿūd’s report urging people to use honey and the Qurʾān as the two cures.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p186/r2.anchor: نعم كون القرآن شفاء مما لا كلام فيه وقد أخرج الطبراني وغيره عن ابن مسعود عليكم بالشفاءين العسل والقرآن

ALUSI-FULL:v14p186/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p186/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v14p186/r3.claim: The passage mentions water first because it is more useful and fundamental to milk and the later foods; milk follows because it is needed more than the others and can replace water.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p186/r3.anchor: وقدم سبحانه الأخبار عن إنزال الماء لما أن الماء أتم نفعا وأعظم شأنا وهو أصل أصيل لتكون اللبن وما بعده ثم ذكر اللبن لأنه يحتاج إليه أكثر من غيره

ALUSI-FULL:v14p186/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p186/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v14p186/r4.claim: Al-Ālūsī says he witnessed some ascetics abandon water for years, relying on milk, and heard a similar account about Bedouin leaders; he treats this as evidence of milk’s naturalness.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p186/r4.anchor: فقد ترك شرب الماء عدة من السنين مكتفيا بشرب اللبن وسمعنا نحو ذلك عن بعض رؤساء الأعراب وهو الدليل على الفطرة

ALUSI-FULL:v14p186/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p186/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v14p186/r5.claim: The Prophet chose milk when offered milk, wine, and honey during the Night Journey.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p186/r5.anchor: ولذلك اختاره صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم حين أسري به وعرض عليه مع الخمر والعسل

ALUSI-FULL:v14p186/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p186/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v14p186/r6.claim: Wine follows milk because it is closer to water as grape juice, whereas honey often serves as bread’s accompaniment; milk and wine also resemble one another in coming from dense matter, yet contrast in ease of swallowing.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p186/r6.anchor: ثم الخمر لأنها أقرب إلى الماء من العسل فإنها ماء العنب ولم يعهد جعلها إداما كالعسل فإنه كثيرا مايؤدم به الخبز ويؤكل

ALUSI-FULL:v14p186/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p186/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v14p186/r7.claim: The sequence also contrasts wine, which became forbidden after its verse was revealed, with milk, whose drinking remained permitted; this strengthens the contrast between them.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p186/r7.anchor: وشرب اللبن لم يزل سائغا وبذلك يقوي التضاد

ALUSI-FULL:v14p186/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p186/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v14p186/r8.claim: Al-Ālūsī finds the placement of “good provision” after wine and before honey self-evident, and says his rationale for wine after milk and before honey is stronger than any case for honey preceding wine.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p186/r8.anchor: وأما ذكر الرزق الحسن بعد الخمر وتقديمه على العسل فالوجه فيه ظاهر جدا ولعل ما اعتبرناه في وجه تقديم الخمر على العسل وذكره بعد اللبن أقوى

ALUSI-FULL:v14p186/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p186/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v14p186/r9.claim: The sequence of water, milk, wine, and honey parallels the description of Paradise’s rivers in another verse.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p186/r9.anchor: وقد جاء ذكر الماء واللبن والخمر والعسل في وصف الجنة على هذا الترتيب

ALUSI-FULL:v14p186/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p186/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v14p186/r10.claim: “In that” points to the described signs of divine power, which constitute a great sign for people who reflect.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p186/r10.anchor: إن في ذلك ( المذكور من آثار قدرة الله تعالى ( لآية ( عظيمة ( لقوم يتفكرون

ALUSI-FULL:v14p187/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p187/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v14p187/r1.claim: Reflecting on the bee’s precise knowledge and astonishing actions, the sweet drink’s varied colors, and its healing property proves that a wise, powerful Lord inspired and equipped the bee; the verse therefore ends by urging reflection.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p187/r1.anchor: فإن من تفكر في اختصاص النحل بتلك العلوم الدقيقة والأفعال العجيبة التي مرت الإشارة إليها وخروج هذا الشراب الحلو المختلف الألوان وتضمنه الشفاء

ALUSI-FULL:v14p187/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p187/r2.speaker: الرافضة
ALUSI-FULL:v14p187/r2.claim: Al-Ālūsī ridicules an allegory reported in al-Kashshāf that identifies the bees with ʿAlī and his followers; a courtier called Banū Hāshim’s knowledge something emerging from their bellies and was answered with a scatological joke.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p187/r2.anchor: ومن بدع تأويلات الرافضة على ما في الكشاف أن المراد بالنحل علي كرم الله تعالى وجهه وقومه

ALUSI-FULL:v14p187/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p187/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v14p187/r3.claim: Al-Ālūsī signals that the Sufis’ interpretation in the section on allusive readings will be discussed later.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p187/r3.anchor: وستسمع إن شاء الله تعالى ما يقوله الصوفية قدس الله تعالى أسرارهم في باب الإشارة

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p29#2/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p29#2/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p29#2/r4.claim: The phrase 'all fruits' is not literally universal, as in the expression about the Queen of Sheba being given everything in 27:23.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p29#2/r4.anchor: ليس معنى الكل العموم، وهو كقوله تعالى: "وأوتيت من كل شيء" (النمل-23)

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p29#2/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p29#2/r5.speaker: unnamed view
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p29#2/r5.claim: Some take 'submissive' as describing the paths: they are made easy for bees to travel.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p29#2/r5.anchor: قيل: هي نعت الطرق، يقول: هي مذللة للنحل سهلة المسالك.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p29#2/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p29#2/r6.speaker: مجاهد
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p29#2/r6.claim: Mujahid says no place a bee travels is rough or difficult for it.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p29#2/r6.anchor: قال مجاهد: لا يتوعر عليها مكان سلكته.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p29#2/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p29#2/r7.speaker: unnamed view
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p29#2/r7.claim: Others take 'submissive' as describing bees, obedient under divine control as their keeper moves them.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p29#2/r7.anchor: وقال آخرون: الذلل نعت النحل، أي: مطيعة منقادة بالتسخير. يقال: إن أربابها ينقلونها من مكان إلى مكان

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p29#2/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p29#2/r8.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p29#2/r8.claim: The account says bees have a leader: when it stops, they stop, and when it moves, they move.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p29#2/r8.anchor: ولها يعسوب إذا وقف وقفت وإذا سار سارت.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p29#3/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p29#3/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p29#3/r1.claim: The drink is honey, whose colors include white, red, and yellow; its healing is in the honey, which the author prefers over Mujahid's Quran interpretation.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p29#3/r1.anchor: يعني: العسل {مختلف ألوانه} أبيض وأحمر وأصفر. {فيه شفاء للناس} أي: في العسل. وقال مجاهد: أي في القرآن، والأول أولى.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p29#3/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p29#3/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p29#3/r2.claim: In Abu Sa'id's report, the Prophet repeatedly prescribes honey for a man's brother's diarrhea, then says God spoke truly and the brother's belly falsely; the man gives honey again and his brother recovers.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p29#3/r2.anchor: عن أبي سعيد الخدري قال: جاء رجل إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال: إن أخي استطلق بطنه، فقال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: اسقه عسلا

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p29#3/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p29#3/r3.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p29#3/r3.claim: Ibn Mas'ud says honey cures every illness and the Quran cures what is in people's hearts.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p29#3/r3.anchor: قال عبد الله بن مسعود: العسل شفاء من كل داء، والقرآن شفاء لما في الصدور

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p29#3/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p29#3/r4.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p29#3/r4.claim: A further narration from Ibn Mas'ud urges using the two cures, the Quran and honey.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p29#3/r4.anchor: وروي عنه أنه قال عليكم بالشفاءين القرآن والعسل

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p30/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p30/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p30/r1.claim: People who reflect take the sign as a lesson.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p30/r1.anchor: إن في ذلك لآية لقوم يتفكرون} فيعتبرون.

BAYDAWI-FULL:16:68-69/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:16:68-69/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:16:68-69/r6.claim: The bees eat whatever fruits they desire, bitter or sweet.
BAYDAWI-FULL:16:68-69/r6.anchor: من كل ثمرة تشتهينها مرها وحلوها

BAYDAWI-FULL:16:68-69/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:16:68-69/r7.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:16:68-69/r7.claim: The bee follows what it ate along divine pathways where God's power transforms bitter light into honey inside it; alternatively, it follows the paths taught for making honey, or easily and unconfused returns along God's routes to its hives.
BAYDAWI-FULL:16:68-69/r7.anchor: في مسالكه التي يحيل فيها بقدرته النور المر عسلا من أجوافك

BAYDAWI-FULL:16:68-69/r8.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:16:68-69/r8.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:16:68-69/r8.claim: Dhululan may describe the paths as made easy by God, or describe the bee as obedient and compliant.
BAYDAWI-FULL:16:68-69/r8.anchor: جمع ذلول وهي حال من السبل، أي مذللة ذللها الله تعالى

BAYDAWI-FULL:16:68-69/r9.author: al-Bayḍāwī
