QURTUBI-FULL:16:69#5/r7.anchor: قال أبو عيسى: في إسناده مقال، ولا يصح عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في هذا الباب كبير شيء

QURTUBI-FULL:16:69#5/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:16:69#5/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:16:69#5/r8.claim: Qurtubi says most scholars follow the stated ruling and names Ahmad and Ishaq among them; some scholars say honey has no zakat.
QURTUBI-FULL:16:69#5/r8.anchor: والعمل على هذا عند أكثر أهل العلم، وبه يقول أحمد وإسحاق، وقال بعض أهل العلم: ليس في العسل شيء.

QURTUBI-FULL:16:69#5/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:16:69#5/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:16:69#5/r9.claim: Reflection on bees' marvelous skill despite their frail bodies leads to certainty that God inspires their craft.
QURTUBI-FULL:16:69#5/r9.anchor: فيشهد اليقين بأن ملهمها الصنعة اللطيفة مع البنية الضعيفة، وحذقها باحتيالها في تفاوت أحوالها هو الله سبحانه وتعالى كما قال: { وأوحى ربك إلى النحل }.

QURTUBI-FULL:16:69#5/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:16:69#5/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:16:69#5/r10.claim: Bees eat sour, bitter, sweet, salty, and harmful plants, yet God makes their output sweet honey and healing, demonstrating divine power.
QURTUBI-FULL:16:69#5/r10.anchor: ثم أنها تأكل الحامض والمر والحلو والمالح والحشائش الضارة، فيجعله الله تعالى عسلا حلوا وشفاء، وفي هذا دليل على قدرته.

QURTUBI-FULL:16:69#5/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:16:69#5/r11.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:16:69#5/r11.claim: Alternatively, the warning may concern ruqyas outside God's Book; the Qur'an is healing, and the Prophet performed ruqya and instructed companions to do so.
QURTUBI-FULL:16:69#5/r11.anchor: وقد قال سبحانه وتعالى { وننزل من القرآن ما هو شفآء }

RAZI-FULL:v20p58/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v20p58/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v20p58/r1.claim: Min in 'eat from all fruits' may be partitive or may mark the starting point/source.
RAZI-FULL:v20p58/r1.anchor: لفظة ( من ) ههنا للتبعيض أو لابتداء الغاية

RAZI-FULL:v20p58/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v20p58/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v20p58/r2.claim: Al-Razi cites medical books for a theory that fine dew forms in the air at night and falls on tree leaves, sometimes as tiny scattered particles and sometimes in visible quantity.
RAZI-FULL:v20p58/r2.anchor: ورأيت في ( كتب الطب ) أنه تعالى دبر هذا العالم على وجه ، وهو أنه يحدث في الهواء طل لطيف في الليالي

RAZI-FULL:v20p58/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v20p58/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v20p58/r3.claim: Visible accumulated dew is called taranjabin; in some countries it collects on the tips of tamarisk trees.
RAZI-FULL:v20p58/r3.anchor: أما القسم الثاني : فهو مثل الترنجبين فإنه طل ينزل من الهواء ويجتمع على أطراف الطرفاء في بعض البلدان وذلك محسوس

RAZI-FULL:v20p58/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v20p58/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v20p58/r4.claim: On the fine-dew theory, bees are inspired to collect honeyed particles from flowers and leaves, eat some for nourishment, and carry more to the hive to store as honey.
RAZI-FULL:v20p58/r4.anchor: فهو الذي ألهم الله تعالى هذا النحل حتى أنها تلتقط تلك الذرات من الأزهار وأوراق الأشجار بأفواهها

RAZI-FULL:v20p58/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v20p58/r5.speaker: بعض الناس
RAZI-FULL:v20p58/r5.claim: Another account says bees eat fragrant flowers and leaves, God transforms them into honey inside their bodies, and they then vomit it out.
RAZI-FULL:v20p58/r5.anchor: ومن الناس من يقول : إن النحل تأكل من الأزهار الطيبة والأوراق المعطرة أشياء ، ثم إنه تعالى يقلب تلك الأجسام في داخل بدنها عسلا

RAZI-FULL:v20p58/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v20p58/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v20p58/r6.claim: Al-Razi prefers the first account as more rational and inductively plausible: taranjabin resembles honey and is known to form as dew on trees and flowers.
RAZI-FULL:v20p58/r6.anchor: والقول الأول أقرب إلى العقل وأشد مناسبة إلى الاستقراء ، فإن طبيعة الترنجبين قريبة من العسل في الطعم والشكل

RAZI-FULL:v20p58/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v20p58/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v20p58/r7.claim: He adds that bees feed on honey, since people leave some in the hive after harvesting it; this supports their gathering the honeyed dew particles as food.
RAZI-FULL:v20p58/r7.anchor: فنحن نشاهد أن هذا النحل إنما يتغذى بالعسل ، ولذلك فإنا إذا استخرجنا العسل من بيوت النحل نترك لها بقية

RAZI-FULL:v20p58/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v20p58/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v20p58/r8.claim: On the account he prefers, min means the fruits are the source from which the bees eat, rather than a partitive selection.
RAZI-FULL:v20p58/r8.anchor: قوله تعالى : { ثم كلى من كل الثمرات } كلمة ( من ) ههنا تكون لابتداء الغاية ، ولا تكون للتبعيض

RAZI-FULL:v20p58#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v20p58#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v20p58#2/r1.claim: One reading is that after eating whatever fruit she desires, the bee follows the routes God taught her for making honey.
RAZI-FULL:v20p58#2/r1.anchor: ثم كلي كل ثمرة تشتهينها فإذا أكلتها فاسلكي سبل ربك في الطرق التي ألهمك وأفهمك في عمل العسل

RAZI-FULL:v20p58#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v20p58#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v20p58#2/r2.claim: Alternatively, the bee is told to follow God's routes while seeking fruit.
RAZI-FULL:v20p58#2/r2.anchor: أو يكون المراد : فاسلكي في طلب تلك الثمرات سبل ربك

RAZI-FULL:v20p58#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v20p58#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v20p58#2/r3.claim: Dhululan may describe the paths, which God has made easy and accessible to the bee, as in 67:15.
RAZI-FULL:v20p58#2/r3.anchor: أنه حال من السبل لأن الله تعالى ذللها لها ووطأها وسهلها ، كقوله : { هو الذى جعل لكم الارض ذلولا } ( الملك : 15 )

RAZI-FULL:v20p58#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v20p58#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v20p58#2/r4.claim: Alternatively, dhululan describes the bee as docile and compliant with what it has been commanded.
RAZI-FULL:v20p58#2/r4.anchor: أنه حال من الضمير في { فاسلكى } أي وأنت أيها النحل ذلل منقادة لما أمرت به

RAZI-FULL:v20p58#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v20p58#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v20p58#2/r5.claim: The wording shifts from addressing the bee to speaking about it because the passage now addresses human beings and argues from the bee's marvels to God's power, wisdom and governance.
RAZI-FULL:v20p58#2/r5.anchor: أن المقصود من ذكر هذه الأحوال أن يحتج الإنسان المكلف به على قدرة الله تعالى وحكمته

RAZI-FULL:v20p58#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v20p58#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v20p58#2/r6.claim: If honey is collected dew carried in bees' mouths, 'from their bellies' means from their mouths; any cavity inside a body can be called a belly, as with the cavities of the brain.
RAZI-FULL:v20p58#2/r6.anchor: وكل تجويف في داخل البدن فإنه يسمى بطنا ، ألا ترى أنهم يقولون : بطون الدماغ

RAZI-FULL:v20p58#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v20p58#2/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v20p58#2/r7.claim: On the ordinary account that bees eat leaves and fruits and then vomit honey, the phrase 'from their bellies' is straightforward.
RAZI-FULL:v20p58#2/r7.anchor: وأما على قول أهل الظاهر ، وهو أن النحلة تأكل الأوراق والثمرات ثم تقيء فذلك هو العسل فالكلام ظاهر

RAZI-FULL:v20p58#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v20p58#2/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v20p58#2/r8.claim: Honey is a drink because it is consumed on its own and also made into beverages.
RAZI-FULL:v20p58#2/r8.anchor: فالصفة الأولى : كونه شرابا والأمر كذلك ، لأنه تارة يشرب وحده وتارة يتخذ من الأشربة

RAZI-FULL:v20p58#2/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v20p58#2/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v20p58#2/r9.claim: Honey comes in red, white and yellow varieties; comparison with the differently colored mountains in 35:27 shows that the colors are governed by a choosing agent, not by nature.
RAZI-FULL:v20p58#2/r9.anchor: ونظيره قوله تعالى : { ومن الجبال جدد بيض وحمر مختلف ألوانها وغرابيب سود } ( فاطر : 27 ) والمقصود منه : إبطال القول بالطبع

RAZI-FULL:v20p59/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v20p59/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v20p59/r1.claim: Al-Razi's correct interpretation is that 'in it is healing for people' describes honey.
RAZI-FULL:v20p59/r1.anchor: القول الأول : وهو الصحيح أنه صفة للعسل

RAZI-FULL:v20p59/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v20p59/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v20p59/r2.claim: Honey's harm to some people or conditions does not disprove the verse: it does not claim to heal everyone, every illness, or in every circumstance, and healing some people from some ailments suffices.
RAZI-FULL:v20p59/r2.anchor: لم يقل إنه شفاء لكل الناس ولكل داء وفي كل حال ، بل لما كان شفاء للبعض

RAZI-FULL:v20p59/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v20p59/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v20p59/r3.claim: Honey's therapeutic value is shown by its role in perfecting nearly every electuary and by the great benefit of honey drinks for phlegmatic illnesses.
RAZI-FULL:v20p59/r3.anchor: والذي يدل على أنه شفاء في الجملة أنه قال معجون من المعاجين إلا وتمامه وكماله إنما يحصل بالعجن بالعسل

RAZI-FULL:v20p59/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v20p59/r4.speaker: مجاهد
RAZI-FULL:v20p59/r4.claim: Mujahid interprets the healing as the Qur'an's healing from unbelief and innovation, taking the honey story to end before this phrase.
RAZI-FULL:v20p59/r4.anchor: والقول الثاني : وهو قول مجاهد أن المراد : أن القرآن شفاء للناس

RAZI-FULL:v20p59/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v20p59/r5.speaker: ابن مسعود
RAZI-FULL:v20p59/r5.claim: Ibn Masud is reported to say that honey heals every disease and the Qur'an heals what is in people's hearts.
RAZI-FULL:v20p59/r5.anchor: وعن ابن مسعود : أن العسل شفاء من كل داء ، والقرآن شفاء لما في الصدور

RAZI-FULL:v20p59/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v20p59/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v20p59/r6.claim: Al-Razi rejects the Qur'an interpretation because the pronoun should refer to the nearest antecedent, the colored drink, and the Qur'an has not been mentioned.
RAZI-FULL:v20p59/r6.anchor: أن الضمير في قوله : { فيه شفآء للناس } يجب عوده إلى أقرب المذكورات

RAZI-FULL:v20p59/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v20p59/r7.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
RAZI-FULL:v20p59/r7.claim: Abu Sa'id reports that a man brought his brother's stomach complaint to the Prophet, who repeatedly prescribed honey until the brother recovered; the report supports honey as the referent.
RAZI-FULL:v20p59/r7.anchor: ما روى أبو سعيد الخدري : أنه جاء رجل إلى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وقال : إن أخي يشتكي بطنه

RAZI-FULL:v20p60/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v20p60/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v20p60/r1.claim: Al-Razi explains the Prophet's 'God spoke truth and your brother's belly lied' by saying the Prophet knew through revelation that honey would help later, although it had not helped yet.
RAZI-FULL:v20p60/r1.anchor: لعله عليه السلام علم بنور الوحي أن ذلك العسل سيظهر نفعه بعد ذلك

RAZI-FULL:v20p60/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v20p60/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v20p60/r2.claim: The bee's precise knowledge, including its hexagonal cells and other remarkable behaviors, is a sign of God's wisdom.
RAZI-FULL:v20p60/r2.anchor: اختصاص النحل بتلك العلوم الدقيقة والمعارف الغامضة مثل بناء البيوت المسدسة وسائر الأحوال

RAZI-FULL:v20p60/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v20p60/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v20p60/r3.claim: The bees' ability to find honey-producing particles on the tips of trees and leaves is a sign of divine design.
RAZI-FULL:v20p60/r3.anchor: اهتداؤها إلى جميع تلك الأجزاء العسلية من أطراف الأشجار والأوراق

RAZI-FULL:v20p60/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v20p60/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v20p60/r4.claim: God creates beneficial particles in the air, deposits them on leaves and trees, then inspires bees to gather them; this ordered process shows the world's wise design.
RAZI-FULL:v20p60/r4.anchor: خلق الله تعالى الأجزاء النافعة في جو الهواء ، ثم إلقاؤها على أطراف الأشجار والأوراق ، ثم إلهام النحل إلى جمعها

STUDYQURAN:16:68/r11.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:16:68/r11.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:16:68/r11.claim: The drink of diverse hues from the bees' bellies is honey, which the verse calls healing for people.
STUDYQURAN:16:68/r11.anchor: The drink of diverse hues that comes forth from their bellies is honey (Z), wherein there is healing for mankind

STUDYQURAN:16:68/r12.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:16:68/r12.speaker: al-Qurṭubī
STUDYQURAN:16:68/r12.claim: Al-Qurṭubī reads the verse as generally legitimating medical treatment against the view that illness should simply be endured as God's decree.
STUDYQURAN:16:68/r12.anchor: this verse legitimates and makes permissable in a general way seeking medicinal treatments for physical ailments

STUDYQURAN:16:68/r13.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:16:68/r13.speaker: the Prophet
STUDYQURAN:16:68/r13.claim: When a man reported his brother's stomach ailment, the Prophet prescribed honey; after the first dose failed, he repeated the instruction, said God's truth outlasted the brother's stomach's false report, and the brother recovered.
STUDYQURAN:16:68/r13.anchor: The Prophet again instructed the man to feed his brother honey, saying, “God speaks the truth

STUDYQURAN:16:68/r14.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:16:68/r14.speaker: Sufi commentators
STUDYQURAN:16:68/r14.claim: A knower and seeker who follows God's ways may become, like the bee, a source of spiritual healing for others.
STUDYQURAN:16:68/r14.anchor: a knower and seeker of God who follows the ways and commands of the Lord, as does the bee, will, like the bee, become a source of spiritual healing for others

STUDYQURAN:16:68/r15.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:16:68/r15.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:16:68/r15.claim: The Quran is also described as a source of healing for humanity.
STUDYQURAN:16:68/r15.anchor: The Quran is also described as a source of healing for humanity (10:57; 17:82)

STUDYQURAN:16:68/r16.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:16:68/r16.speaker: the Prophet
STUDYQURAN:16:68/r16.claim: A hadith calls honey a cure for every ailment and the Quran a cure for what is in people's breasts, commending both cures.
STUDYQURAN:16:68/r16.anchor: Honey is the cure for every ailment, and the Quran is the cure for that which lies within breasts

STUDYQURAN:16:68/r17.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:16:68/r17.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:16:68/r17.claim: Both healings come through waḥy, symbolically in the bee's case.
STUDYQURAN:16:68/r17.anchor: both of which come about, according to the Quran, through waḥy, or “revelation,” at least symbolically in the case of the bee

STUDYQURAN:16:68/r18.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:16:68/r18.speaker: Ibn ʿAbbās
STUDYQURAN:16:68/r18.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reports that the Prophet prohibited killing bees and other animals praised in the Quran, including ants.
STUDYQURAN:16:68/r18.anchor: reported from Ibn ʿAbbās that the Prophet forbade his followers to kill bees and other animals mentioned favorably

STUDYQURAN:16:68/r19.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:16:68/r19.speaker: Mālikī school and some al-Shāfiʿī interpretations
STUDYQURAN:16:68/r19.claim: These legal interpretations exempt honey from obligatory zakāh.
STUDYQURAN:16:68/r19.anchor: According to the Mālikī school of law and some interpretations of al-Shāfiʿī’s view, honey is exempt from the mandatory alms

STUDYQURAN:16:68/r20.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:16:68/r20.speaker: some Shiite commentators
STUDYQURAN:16:68/r20.claim: Some Shiite readings take the bee as ʿAlī and the Prophet's family, and its diverse drink as Quranic knowledge and wisdom in their teachings that heals spiritually.
STUDYQURAN:16:68/r20.anchor: the bee here is a reference to ʿAlīand the family of the Prophet, and the drink of diverse hues refers symbolically to the knowledge of the Quran

STUDYQURAN:16:68/r21.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:16:68/r21.speaker: al-Qurṭubī and al-Zamakhsharī
STUDYQURAN:16:68/r21.claim: Al-Qurṭubī and al-Zamakhsharī note this Shiite interpretation but reject its soundness.
STUDYQURAN:16:68/r21.anchor: although its soundness is refuted by them

STUDYQURAN:16:68/r22.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:16:68/r22.speaker: al-Ṭabrisī
STUDYQURAN:16:68/r22.claim: Al-Ṭabrisī traces the interpretation to ʿAlī saying he was the believers' yaʿsūb, a term meaning both male bee and leader or chieftain.
STUDYQURAN:16:68/r22.anchor: al-Ṭabrisī indicates that this interpretation derives from ʿAlī’s statement that he was the yaʿsūb of the believers

SAMIN-DURR:16:69/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:16:69/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:16:69/r1.claim: ذللا is the plural of ذلول.

SAMIN-DURR:16:69/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:16:69/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:16:69/r2.claim: It may be a circumstantial accusative of the paths, which God made subservient, as in 67:15.
SAMIN-DURR:16:69/r2.anchor: ويجوز أن تكون حالا من السبل، أي: ذللها الله تعالى، كقوله:

SAMIN-DURR:16:69/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:16:69/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:16:69/r3.claim: Alternatively, it is a circumstantial accusative of the bee as subject of اسلكي, meaning obedient and compliant; both interpretations occur in tafsir.
SAMIN-DURR:16:69/r3.anchor: وأن تكون حالا من فاعل " اسلكي " ، أي: مطيعة منقادة. وفي التفسير المعنيان منقولان.

SAMIN-DURR:16:69/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:16:69/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:16:69/r4.claim: سبل may be adverbial: the bee follows what it ate through the Lord's pathways where divine power transforms it into honey.
SAMIN-DURR:16:69/r4.anchor: وانتصاب " سبل " يجوز أن يكون على الظرفية، أي: فاسلكي ما أكلت في سبل ربك

SAMIN-DURR:16:69/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:16:69/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:16:69/r5.claim: Alternatively, سبل is the direct object: paths God taught and showed the bee for making honey.
SAMIN-DURR:16:69/r5.anchor: وأن يكون مفعولا به، أي: اسلكي الطرق التي أفهمك وعلمك في عمل العسل.

SAMIN-DURR:16:69/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:16:69/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:16:69/r6.claim: من كل الثمرات may be partitive; its alternative means the bee eats a manna-like substance descending onto leaves, not the fruit itself, which he calls very remote.
SAMIN-DURR:16:69/r6.anchor: و " من " في { من كل الثمرات } يجوز ان تكون تبعيضية، وأن تكون للابتداء على معنى:

SAMIN-DURR:16:69/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:16:69/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:16:69/r7.claim: يخرج من بطونها shifts person; continuing the earlier address would have said من بطونك.
SAMIN-DURR:16:69/r7.anchor: قوله: { يخرج من بطونها } التفات وإخبار بذلك، ولو جاء على الكلام الأول لقيل: من بطونك.

SAMIN-DURR:16:69/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:16:69/r8.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:16:69/r8.claim: The pronoun in فيه most naturally refers to شراب; another view refers it to the Qur'an.
SAMIN-DURR:16:69/r8.anchor: والهاء في / " فيه " تعود على " شراب " ، وهو الظاهر، وقيل: تعود على القرآن.

TAB-FULL:v14p286#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v14p286#2/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v14p286#2/r5.claim: He says God commanded the bees to eat fruits and follow their Lord's paths gently.
TAB-FULL:v14p286#2/r5.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قوله: {وأوحى ربك إلى النحل} [النحل: 68] الآية، قال: «أمرها أن تأكل من الثمرات

TAB-FULL:v14p287/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v14p287/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v14p287/r1.claim: He says dhululan means made easy and that dhull is the plural of dhalul; the interpreters agree with this gloss.
TAB-FULL:v14p287/r1.anchor: والذلل: جمع ذلول. وبنحو الذي قلنا في ذلك قال أهل التأويل

TAB-FULL:v14p287/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v14p287/r2.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v14p287/r2.claim: He says the bees find no rough or difficult place along a path they take.
TAB-FULL:v14p287/r2.anchor: عن مجاهد، في قول الله تعالى: {فاسلكي سبل ربك ذللا} [النحل: 69] قال: «لا يتوعر عليها مكان سلكته»

TAB-FULL:v14p287/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v14p287/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v14p287/r3.claim: On Mujahid's reading, dhululan describes the paths; the phrase is effectively “easy for you,” with the definite article omitted and the word used circumstantially.
TAB-FULL:v14p287/r3.anchor: الذلل من نعت السبل. والتأويل على قوله: {فاسلكي سبل ربك ذللا} [النحل: 69] الذلل لك

TAB-FULL:v14p287/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v14p287/r4.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v14p287/r4.anchor: عن قتادة، قوله: " {فاسلكي سبل ربك ذللا} [النحل: 69] أي مطيعة "

TAB-FULL:v14p287/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v14p287/r5.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v14p287/r5.claim: He applies dhululan to the bees: they are tame and follow their keepers as they are taken to forage, as with livestock made docile for people.
TAB-FULL:v14p287/r5.anchor: قال ابن زيد، في قوله: {فاسلكي سبل ربك ذللا} [النحل: 69] قال: " الذلول الذي يقاد ويذهب به حيث أراد صاحبه

TAB-FULL:v14p287/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v14p287/r6.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v14p287/r6.claim: Both grammatical readings are sound, but he prefers dhululan to describe the paths because they are nearer in the sentence.
TAB-FULL:v14p287/r6.anchor: وكلا القولين غير بعيد من الصواب في الصحة وجهان مخرجان، غير أنا اخترنا أن يكون نعتا للسبل لأنها إليها أقرب

TAB-FULL:v14p289/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v14p289/r1.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v14p289/r1.claim: He takes the healing pronoun to refer to the Qur'an, which heals people.
TAB-FULL:v14p289/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد: {فيه شفاء للناس} [النحل: 69] قال: «في القرآن شفاء»

TAB-FULL:v14p289/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v14p289/r2.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v14p289/r2.claim: He takes the healing as honey's cure for illnesses and says bees were not to be split apart or killed.
TAB-FULL:v14p289/r2.anchor: عن قتادة، قوله: {يخرج من بطونها شراب مختلف ألوانه، فيه شفاء للناس} [النحل: 69] ففيه شفاء كما قال الله تعالى من الأدواء

TAB-FULL:v14p289/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v14p289/r3.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v14p289/r3.claim: He reports that the Prophet prescribed honey for a man's brother's stomach ailment; after an initial worsening, another dose cured him.
TAB-FULL:v14p289/r3.anchor: عن قتادة، قال: جاء رجل إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم، فذكر أن أخاه اشتكى بطنه، فقال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

TAB-FULL:v14p289/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v14p289/r4.speaker: عبد الله
TAB-FULL:v14p289/r4.claim: He says there are two cures: honey for every disease and the Qur'an for what is in people's breasts.
TAB-FULL:v14p289/r4.anchor: عن عبد الله، قال: " شفاءان: العسل شفاء من كل داء، والقرآن شفاء لما في الصدور "

TAB-FULL:v14p289/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v14p289/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v14p289/r5.claim: He identifies the substance that heals people as honey.
TAB-FULL:v14p289/r5.anchor: عن ابن عباس: " {فيه شفاء للناس} [النحل: 69] العسل "

TAB-FULL:v14p289/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v14p289/r6.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v14p289/r6.claim: He prefers honey as the referent of “in it,” because the pronoun occurs in a passage discussing honey.
TAB-FULL:v14p289/r6.anchor: فأن تكون الهاء من ذكر العسل، إذ كانت في سياق الخبر عنه أولى من غيره

ZAJJAJ:v3p210/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p210/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p210/r1.claim: Honey exits through the bee’s mouth, but is attributed to the bellies because food is transformed there; bees move it from belly to mouth, as humans release saliva from the mouth.
ZAJJAJ:v3p210/r1.anchor: لأن استحالة الأطعمة لا تكون إلا في البطون فيخرج بعضها من الفم

ZAJJAJ:v3p210/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p210/r2.speaker: قيل
ZAJJAJ:v3p210/r2.claim: One view makes the pronoun in ‘in it is healing’ refer to honey, so the verse says honey heals people.
ZAJJAJ:v3p210/r2.anchor: قيل إن. الهاء يرجع على العسل، المعنى في العسل شفاء للناس.

ZAJJAJ:v3p210/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p210/r3.speaker: قيل
ZAJJAJ:v3p210/r3.claim: Another view makes the pronoun refer to the Qur’an: its account of bees and other narratives that show God’s oneness heals people.
ZAJJAJ:v3p210/r3.anchor: وقيل إن الهاء للقرآن، المعنى في القرآن شفاء للناس

ZAJJAJ:v3p210/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p210/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p210/r4.claim: The honey interpretation is very good; although honey can harm some, water can also kill depending on bodily illness, and many remedies and drinks are based on honey.

ZAJJAJ:v3p210/r5.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p210/r5.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p210/r5.claim: Only the ignorant deny honey’s healing; anyone who understands its benefit, even outside this religious community, acknowledges that honey heals.
ZAJJAJ:v3p210/r5.anchor: وهذا الاعتراض في أمر العسل إنما هو اعتراض جهلة لا يعرفون قدرة في النفع،

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p122/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p122/r1.speaker: ابن قتيبة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p122/r1.claim: The command to eat from all fruits is not universal in scope, as in the Quran's statements that the Queen was given everything and that the wind destroyed everything.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p122/r1.anchor: قال ابن قتيبة: أي من الثمرات، وكل هاهنا لا يقع على العموم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p122/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p122/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p122/r2.claim: The bee follows its Lord's paths by seeking pasture along them.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p122/r2.anchor: قال ابن عباس: يريد طرق ربك (¬5)، تطلب فيها الرعي

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p122/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p122/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p122/r3.claim: Dhululan is the plural of dhalūl, meaning yielding, gentle, or subdued; it is also said of a compliant horse.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p122/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p122/r4.speaker: مجاهد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p122/r4.claim: Mujāhid says no place the bee travels becomes rough or difficult for it; on this reading dhululan describes the paths.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p122/r4.anchor: قال مجاهد: لا يتوعر عليها مكان سلكته (¬2)، فعلى هذا الذلل من صفة السبل

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p122/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p122/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p122/r5.claim: The author finds it more apt that God has made the bee's routes easy, an interpretation chosen by al-Zajjāj.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p122/r5.anchor: الأشبه: لا تتوعر عليها لتذليل الله لها إياها

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p122/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p122/r6.speaker: قتادة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p122/r6.claim: Qatāda takes dhululan to mean obedient; Ibn Qutayba chooses this because the bees are subdued by God's control.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p122/r6.anchor: وقال قتادة: ذللا يعني مطيعة (¬5)، وهو اختيار ابن قتيبة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p122/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p122/r7.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p122/r7.claim: Al-Farrāʾ records both analyses: dhululan can describe the paths or the bees, which are subdued so that the drink issues from their bellies.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p122/r7.anchor: وحكى الفراء القولين، فقال: ذللا نعت للسبيل، ويقال: نعت للنحل

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p124/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p124/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p124/r1.claim: The grammar shifts from addressing the bee directly to reporting about it.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p124/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p124/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p124/r2.claim: The drink's colors include red, white, and yellow.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p124/r2.anchor: قال ابن عباس: منه أحمر وأبيض وأصفر

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p124/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p124/r3.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p124/r3.claim: The bee eats sour, bitter, and otherwise unpalatable things, which God transforms into honey; it expels honey from its mouth like human saliva.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p124/r3.anchor: هي تأكل الحامض والمر وما لا يوصف طعمه فيحيل الله ذلك عسلا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p124/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p124/r4.speaker: أكثر المفسرين
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p124/r4.claim: Most exegetes take the pronoun in فيه back to the drink, honey, and say it contains healing for people.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p124/r4.anchor: أكثر المفسرين على أن الكناية تعود إلى قوله: {شراب}، وهو العسل

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p124/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p124/r5.speaker: الزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p124/r5.claim: Al-Zajjāj answers the objection that honey can harm some people by analogy with water: it sustains life but can kill someone whose illness makes it harmful.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p124/r5.anchor: أجاب عن هذا الزجاج، وقال: الماء حياة كل شيء

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p124/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p124/r6.speaker: السدي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p124/r6.claim: Al-Suddī says honey heals the illnesses for which it is a remedy.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p124/r6.anchor: وهذا معنى قول السدي: فيه شفاء للأوجاع التي شفاؤها فيه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p124/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p124/r7.speaker: مجاهد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p124/r7.claim: Mujāhid interprets the healing as being in the Quran.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p124/r7.anchor: وروي عن مجاهد: {فيه شفاء للناس}: أي في القرآن

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p124/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p124/r8.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p124/r8.claim: Abū Isḥāq says the Quranic account of the bee and other stories is healing because it proves God's oneness, explains lawful and unlawful matters, and removes doubts; this accords with the Quran being healing for hearts.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p124/r8.anchor: فيما قصصنا عليكم من قصة النحل في القرآن وسائر القصص التي تدل على أن الله واحد، شفاء للناس

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p124/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p124/r9.speaker: ابن مسعود
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p124/r9.claim: Ibn Masʿūd says honey cures every disease while the Quran heals what is in people's hearts.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p124/r9.anchor: وقال ابن مسعود: العسل فيه شفاء من كل داء، والقرآن شفاء لما في الصدور

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p124/r10.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p124/r10.speaker: الفراء والزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p124/r10.claim: Al-Farrāʾ and al-Zajjāj transmit both the honey and Quran interpretations of healing.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p124/r11.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p124/r11.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p124/r11.claim: Some prefer the honey interpretation as closer to the apparent wording and cite Abū Saʿīd's report: the Prophet twice told a man to give honey to his sick brother, then said God spoke truth and the brother's belly lied; the brother recovered.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p124/r11.anchor: واختار قوم القول الأول؛ وقالوا: إنه أليق بظاهر الكتاب

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p124/r12.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p124/r12.speaker: النبي ﷺ
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p124/r12.claim: In a report from Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī, the Prophet prescribes honey for the man's brother's stomach illness and says God spoke truth when the repeated dose cures him; the author gives no grading.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p124/r12.anchor: عن أبي سعيد الخدري، قال: جاء رجل إلى النبي -صلى الله عليه وسلم- فقال: إن أخي تشتكي بطنه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p127/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p127/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p127/r1.claim: The sign in the bee's story points to God's greatness and power.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p127/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس: يريد في عظمة الله وقدرته

DAMGHANI:v1p261/r2.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p261/r2.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p261/r2.claim: Sharāb can mean honey, as in the drink of varied colors produced by bees.
DAMGHANI:v1p261/r2.anchor: فوجه منها : الشراب العسل قوله تعالى في سورة النحل

DAMGHANI:v1p184/r1.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p184/r1.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p184/r1.claim: ذللا means subjected or made tractable, as in the subdued fruit clusters and the bees' paths.
DAMGHANI:v1p184/r1.anchor: التذليل التسخير قوله تعالى في سورة الإنسان

BURHAN:v4p318/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p318/r5.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p318/r5.claim: The bee's command to eat من كل الثمرات follows the same rationale, with an added benefit: dates and grapes have already been mentioned immediately before.
BURHAN:v4p318/r5.anchor: وأما قوله تعالى ﴿ ثم كلي من كل الثمرات ﴾ 1 ولم يقل من الثمرات كلها ففيه الحكمة السابقة

BURHAN:v4p318/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p318/r6.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p318/r6.claim: Putting كل before the generic phrase indicates coverage of the whole class, while placing it after can emphasize the entire already specified set, whether generic or definite.
BURHAN:v4p318/r6.anchor: إذا تقدمت اقتضت الإحاطة بالجنس وإذا تأخرت اقتضت الإحاطة بالمؤكد بتمامه جنسا شائعا

BURHAN:v4p320/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p320/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p320/r1.claim: Beginning with كل before the command to eat avoids implying that the fruits refer only to those mentioned earlier and makes the sense comprehensive.
BURHAN:v4p320/r1.anchor: فلو قال بعدها ثم كلي من الثمرات كلها لأوهم أنها للعهد المذكور قبله فكان الابتداء ب كل أحضر للمعنى وأجمع للجنس وأرفع للبس

BURHAN:v1p435/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p435/r1.speaker: القشيري
BURHAN:v1p435/r1.claim: Al-Qushayri reportedly saw the Prophet in a dream while his son was gravely ill; the Prophet directed him to six healing verses, which he recited three times, after which his son recovered.
BURHAN:v1p435/r1.anchor: ويحكى أن الشيخ أبا القاسم القشيري رأى النبى صلى الله عليه وسلم فى المنام

BURHAN:v4p92/r7.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p92/r7.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p92/r7.claim: Healing means that a basic measure of cure is found in it in some cases; the phrase may instead express grandeur.
BURHAN:v4p92/r7.anchor: اذا المعنى انه يحصل فيه اصل الشفاء في جملة صور

ITQAN:v4p333/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p333/r6.speaker: author
ITQAN:v4p333/r6.claim: The Quran encompasses older sciences; medicine maintains health through balance, summarized by moderation, and restores it through the drink with healing, while also treating hearts and breasts.
ITQAN:v4p333/r6.anchor: أما الطب فمداره على حفظ نظام الصحة واستحكام القوة

ITQAN:v3p244/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p244/r10.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p244/r10.claim: Nāqiṣ jinās differs in letter count, with the extra letter at the beginning, middle, or end; examples include sāq/al-masāq and kullī/kulli.
ITQAN:v3p244/r10.anchor: ومنها الناقص بأن يختلف في عدد الحروف سواء كان الحرف المزيد أولا أو وسطا أو آخرا

DAMGHANI:v1p93/r11.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p93/r11.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p93/r11.claim: For bees, thamarāt means blossoms and flowers from which they obtain nourishment.
DAMGHANI:v1p93/r11.anchor: الرابع الثمرات يعني رزق النحل من النور والزهر قوله تعالى في سورة النحل ثم كلي من كل الثمرات يعني النور والورد خاصة
